definition_zh: 深刻的；深远的；深奥的；极度的；深度的（医学）
definition_en: very deep in meaning, knowledge or effect; intense
core_image: 一口井的井底，光只照到井壁上很窄的一圈
scene: 老教授讲完只留一句短话，学生回去想了整晚。Her remark had a profound effect on the whole class.
sceneCN: 这里指影响深入而持久（第 2 个义项：影响深远、强烈而持久）；句意是她那句话对全班产生了深刻影响。

pos.zh: 深刻的；深远的；深奥的；极度的；深部的

senses.title: Deep in meaning
senses.definition: showing deep thought or understanding
senses.definitionCN: 显出深思或深理解的
senses.example: The book offers a profound reading of the poem.
senses.exampleCN: 这本书对这首诗给出了深刻的解读。
senses.why: Latin profundus meant deep like a well, and depth of meaning borrows the same image.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁 profundus 指像井一样的深，意义之深借用了同一意象。

senses.title: Far-reaching in effect
senses.definition: having a strong and lasting influence
senses.definitionCN: 有强烈而持久的影响
senses.example: The discovery had a profound effect on medicine.
senses.exampleCN: 这项发现对医学有深远影响。
senses.why: An effect that reaches the bottom is felt long after the surface event.
senses.whyCN: 触到底部的影响，在表面事件过后很久仍能被感到。

senses.title: Deep in knowledge
senses.definition: showing wide and deep learning
senses.definitionCN: 显出广博而深厚的学识
senses.example: She is a profound scholar of ancient law.
senses.exampleCN: 她是一位研究古代法律的渊博学者。
senses.why: The well image marks a mind that has gone far below the surface.
senses.whyCN: 井的意象标出一个远潜于表面之下的心灵。

senses.title: Intense in feeling
senses.definition: very strong or deeply felt
senses.definitionCN: 非常强烈或感受极深的
senses.example: A profound sadness settled over the room.
senses.exampleCN: 一种深沉的悲伤笼住了屋子。
senses.why: Depth of feeling keeps the physical image but moves it into the body.
senses.whyCN: 情感的深度保留具体意象，却把它移进身体里。

senses.title: Deep sleep or unconsciousness
senses.definition: a state of sleep or lost consciousness from which it is hard to wake
senses.definitionCN: 难以唤醒的深睡或失去意识的状态
senses.example: The patient fell into a profound sleep.
senses.exampleCN: 病人陷入了深度睡眠。
senses.why: Clinical language uses depth literally for states below ordinary waking.
senses.whyCN: 临床用语把「深」按字面用于低于寻常清醒的状态。

senses.title: Deep in physical space
senses.definition: reaching far down or far in from the surface
senses.definitionCN: 从表面向下或向内延伸很远
senses.example: The mine reaches a profound depth.
senses.exampleCN: 这座矿达到很深的深度。
senses.why: This is the oldest layer, where the word still points at a hole.
senses.whyCN: 这是最古老的一层，词仍指着洞。

senses.title: Deep silence or darkness
senses.definition: complete and heavy, as of silence or dark
senses.definitionCN: 指寂静或黑暗，浓重而彻底
senses.example: A profound silence followed the question.
senses.exampleCN: 问题之后是一片深沉的寂静。
senses.why: Anything that feels bottomless can take the word.
senses.whyCN: 凡是让人感到深不见底的事物，都能用这个词。

senses.title: A fundamental change
senses.definition: a change that alters the base of a system, not its surface
senses.definitionCN: 改变系统根基而非表层的变化
senses.example: The reform brought profound change to the courts.
senses.exampleCN: 这场改革给法院带来了根本性变化。
senses.why: Fundus is the bottom, so a profound change touches what everything stands on.
senses.whyCN: fundus 是底部，因此深刻的变化触及万物的立足处。

intro.en: Profound comes from Latin profundus, deep or bottomless, from pro- forward or downward plus fundus, bottom. The source and the internal formation are both clear.
intro.cn: profound 来自拉丁 profundus「深的、无底的」，由 pro-「向前、向下」与 fundus「底部」构成。来源与内部构词都清楚。

items.en: Fundus meant the bottom of a thing and also a farm or estate, the land at the base of a holding.
items.cn: fundus 指物体的底部，也指农庄或地产，即一份产业的根基之地。

items.en: Profundus joined pro- with fundus and meant deep, high in depth, and by extension bottomless.
items.cn: profundus 把 pro- 与 fundus 结合，意为深的、深处很大的，引申为无底的。

items.en: Old French profond carried the adjective into English with the same physical core.
items.cn: 古法语 profond 把这个形容词带进英语，具体核心义保持不变。

items.en: Depth of water became depth of thought, feeling and knowledge without any new word.
items.cn: 水之深变成思想、情感与知识之深，并未另造新词。

items.en: Clinical writing uses profound for sleep or coma, where depth is again literal.
items.cn: 临床写作把 profound 用于睡眠或昏迷，那里的「深」又回到字面。

items.en: Fundus also lies behind foundation and fundamental, which name the base rather than the depth.
items.cn: fundus 也藏在 foundation 与 fundamental 背后，那两个词命名根基而非深度。

note.en: The first group shares the Latin bottom-root; the second group names depth of meaning, feeling or effect.
note.cn: 第一组共享拉丁语「底部」词根；第二组是意义、情感或影响之深的近义说法。

entries.definition: Depth of thought or feeling; the noun from the same adjective.
entries.definitionCN: 思想或情感的深度；同一形容词的名词。

entries.definition: Deeply; to a great degree.
entries.definitionCN: 深深地；极度地。

entries.definition: Serving as a base; from fundus, not a form of profound.
entries.definitionCN: 作为根基的；出自 fundus，不是 profound 的变形。

entries.definition: The base on which something is built.
entries.definitionCN: 建筑物或事物的根基。

entries.definition: Pouring out in great amount; from fundere, to pour, not from fundus.
entries.definitionCN: 大量涌出；出自 fundere「灌注」，与 fundus 无关。

entries.definition: Extending far down or far into a subject.
entries.definitionCN: 向下或向主题内部延伸很远。

entries.definition: Having wide and lasting effects.
entries.definitionCN: 影响宽广而持久。

entries.definition: Very strong in degree.
entries.definitionCN: 程度上非常强烈。

entries.definition: Reaching below the surface, of insight or gaze.
entries.definitionCN: 洞察或目光直达表面之下。

entries.definition: Serious and important, often of words or matters.
entries.definitionCN: 严肃重要，多指言辞或事情。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations use the real Latin parts, the real family and real collocations.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想使用真实的拉丁构件、真实同族词与真实搭配。

normal.en: Fundus is bottom, pro- is downward, so profound is having its bottom far below.
normal.cn: fundus 是底，pro- 是向下，所以 profound 是底在很深的地方。

normal.en: Foundation and fundamental come from fundus, but they name the base, not the depth.
normal.cn: foundation 与 fundamental 出自 fundus，但命名根基，而非深度。

normal.en: Profuse looks close but comes from pouring, not from a bottom.
normal.cn: profuse 形近，却出自「灌注」，不是「底」。

normal.en: Fixed phrases mark the use: profound effect, profound silence, profound sleep.
normal.cn: 固定搭配标出用法：深远影响、深沉寂静、深度睡眠。

normal.en: Profundity is the noun for depth of thought or feeling.
normal.cn: profundity 是思想或情感深度的名词。

abstract.en: Profound is a well whose bottom you cannot see from the rim.
abstract.cn: 深刻是一口从井沿看不见底的井。

abstract.en: A shallow pool can be clear; a deep one holds what light never reaches.
abstract.cn: 浅水可以清澈；深水藏着光到不了的东西。

abstract.en: The word moves from water to thought without changing its shape.
abstract.cn: 这个词从水移到思想，形状始终未变。

examples.en: The lecture left a profound impression on the younger students.
examples.cn: 这场讲座给年轻学生留下了深刻印象。

examples.en: A profound silence followed the reading of the will.
examples.cn: 宣读遗嘱之后是一片深沉的寂静。

examples.en: The war brought profound change to the border towns.
examples.cn: 战争给边境城镇带来了深刻变化。

dict_mnemonic.text: 读作「普若放的」——底放得很深：深刻的

root: 拉丁 profundus「深的、无底的」← pro-「向前、向下」+ fundus「底部」；fundus 也指农庄、地产，并衍生 foundation 与 fundamental，但那两个词指根基而非深度。古法语 profond 传入英语；水的深度转为思想、情感与知识之深，医学又按字面用「深度」。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses descend from the physical well to meaning, effect, learning, feeling, sleep, space, silence and fundamental change.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项从具体的井往下走，依次是意义、影响、学识、情感、睡眠、空间、寂静与根本性变化。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: the bottom of a well, where light reaches only a narrow ring on the wall.
core.cn: 核心意象：井底，光只照到井壁上很窄的一圈。

branches.en: THE DEEP MIND: meaning and learning that go far below the surface.
branches.cn: 深的心智：远潜于表面之下的意义与学识。

branches.en: THE DEEP EFFECT: influence that reaches the base and changes it.
branches.cn: 深的影响：抵达根基并改变它的影响。

branches.en: THE HEAVY FEELING: intense emotion and a silence that feels bottomless.
branches.cn: 沉重的感受：强烈情感与深不见底的寂静。

branches.en: THE DEEP STATE: sleep or coma below ordinary waking.
branches.cn: 深的状态：低于寻常清醒的睡眠或昏迷。

branches.en: THE PHYSICAL DEPTH: a shaft that goes far down.
branches.cn: 具体的深度：向下延伸很远的矿井。

intro.en: Profound is Latin profundus plus the English adjective form; pro- and fundus are both clear.
intro.cn: profound 是拉丁 profundus 加英语形容词形式；pro- 与 fundus 两部分都清楚。

latinIntro.en: Fundus supplies the bottom, pro- stretches it downward, and profundus carries both.
latinIntro.cn: fundus 提供「底部」，pro- 把它向下拉长，profundus 兼有两者。

items.example: The prefix stretches the bottom away from the surface.
items.exampleCN: 前缀把底部从表面向下拉开。

items.example: The stem names what everything stands on.
items.exampleCN: 词干命名万物所立之处。

items.example: The adjective joins the prefix and the bottom.
items.exampleCN: 形容词把前缀与底部合在一起。

items.example: The noun measures the distance to the bottom.
English keeps the adjective and drops the Latin ending.
items.exampleCN: 英语保留形容词，收掉拉丁词尾。

items.example: The adverb marks the degree of an effect.
The noun carries the abstract side.

items.meaning: the base of a building or system
items.example: The family member names the base, not the distance down.
items.exampleCN: 同族词命名根基，而不是向下的距离。

items.example: The adjective belongs to the base line of the family.
items.exampleCN: 这个形容词属于词族的「根基」一支。

items.example: The ending marks the adjective in other Latin borrowings.
items.exampleCN: 这一词尾在别的拉丁借词里标记形容词。

definition_zh: 后代；子女；子孙；（事物的）产物、成果
definition_en: the young or offspring of a person, animal or plant, or the product that something brings forth
core_image: 一株母本植物在温室内分出整齐的幼苗行列，每一行都接着上一代的性状
scene: 温室里，育种者把同一母株的后代逐代排开，记录性状如何分离。Seedlings raised from a single parent plant form one visible progeny.
sceneCN: 这里 progeny 指「同一亲本繁育出的后代群体」（第 1 个义项：人或动植物的后代）；句意为温室里由单一母株育出的幼苗排成一行行，构成一个可见的后代群体。可辨识物件：育苗盘、幼苗、手写标签、温室玻璃。

pos.zh: 后代；子女；子孙（集合名词）

forms.label: 复数（集合名词，形式不变）

senses.title: Offspring of a living thing
senses.definition: the young produced by a person, animal or plant
senses.definitionCN: 人或动物繁育出的幼体
senses.example: The mare's progeny all inherited her calm temperament.
senses.exampleCN: 这匹母马的后代都继承了她沉静的性情。
senses.why: Progeny is a mass noun for what is brought forth, so it treats the young as a collective result rather than counting them one by one.
senses.whyCN: progeny 是把「被生出来之物」当作整体的集合名词，因此把幼体视作一个总的结果，而不是逐个计数。

senses.title: A line of descendants
senses.definition: the whole line of descendants from an ancestor
senses.definitionCN: 从某一祖先延续下来的整条世系
senses.example: The estate passed through his progeny for four generations.
senses.exampleCN: 这座庄园在他的子孙中传了四代。
senses.why: The Latin noun named a line of descent, so English progeny can mean the whole chain, not only the immediate young.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁名词本指一条世系，因此英语 progeny 可以指整条链，而不只是眼前的幼体。

senses.title: Offspring of a plant
senses.definition: the seedlings or bulbs produced by a parent plant
senses.definitionCN: 由母株繁育出的幼苗或球茎
senses.example: Gardeners sell the progeny of that famous rose.
senses.exampleCN: 园艺师出售那株名贵月季的子代。
senses.why: Because plants also beget, the word applies to seedlings and bulbs without any change of form.
senses.whyCN: 植物同样会繁育，因此这个词不加任何词形变化就可用于幼苗与球茎。

senses.title: A product of a cause
senses.definition: something produced as a result of another thing or process
senses.definitionCN: 由另一事物或过程产生的结果
senses.example: The theory is the progeny of two older debates.
senses.exampleCN: 这套理论是两场更早争论的产物。
senses.why: The metaphor treats an idea as a child: what comes forth from a cause is its progeny.
senses.whyCN: 这个隐喻把观念当作孩子：从原因中产出的东西就是它的后代。

senses.title: Successors or followers
senses.definition: the people who continue a tradition or institution
senses.definitionCN: 延续某一传统或机构的人
senses.example: The movement's progeny now run several publishing houses.
senses.exampleCN: 这场运动的后来者如今经营着几家出版社。
senses.why: People who continue a tradition are pictured as its descendants, so the word covers institutional heirs.
senses.whyCN: 延续传统的人被想象成它的子孙，因此这个词也涵盖机构意义上的继承者。

senses.title: Progeny testing in breeding
senses.definition: the practice of judging a parent by the performance of its offspring
senses.definitionCN: 以后代的表现来评判亲本优劣的做法
senses.example: Progeny testing decides which bull is kept for breeding.
senses.exampleCN: 后代测验决定哪头公牛留作种用。
senses.why: In animal breeding the word is fixed in the phrase progeny testing, where the offspring's performance is the evidence.
senses.whyCN: 在畜牧育种中，这个词固定于 progeny testing 这一短语，以子代的表现作为证据。

senses.title: A group taken collectively
senses.titleCN: 作为一个整体看待的后代群
senses.definition: the offspring of one parent considered as a single group
senses.definitionCN: 把同一亲本的后代视作一个整体
senses.example: The whole progeny was raised in the same nursery.
senses.exampleCN: 整批后代都在同一间育苗室中育成。
senses.why: The noun often takes a singular verb because it names a group; this collective reading is why a plural in -ies is unusual.
senses.whyCN: 这个名词常接单数动词，因为它命名的是一个群体；这种集合用法正是它少用 -ies 复数的原因。

senses.title: A legacy carried forward
senses.titleCN: 延续下来的遗产（作品、影响）
senses.definition: the lasting work or influence that survives its source
senses.definitionCN: 在源头之后仍然存续的作品或影响
senses.example: Her progeny is a school of composers who still use her method.
senses.exampleCN: 她留下的传承是一批至今仍用她方法的作曲家。
senses.why: The figurative sense can outlast biology: what survives is not a child but a body of work.
senses.whyCN: 抽象义可以超出生物学：存续下来的不是孩子，而是一整套作品。

intro.en: Progeny came into English through Old French from Latin progenies 'line of descent, offspring', a derivative of progignere 'bring forth', itself pro- 'forth' plus gignere 'beget'.
intro.cn: progeny 经古法语进入英语，源自拉丁 progenies「世系、后代」，由 progignere「向前生出」派生，而后者是 pro-「向前」加 gignere「生育」。

items.en: Gignere 'to beget, bring forth' is the source of genitor and generate. Its pre-Latin form is reconstructed as PIE *ǵenh₁-, so the starred form is a reconstruction rather than a recorded word.
items.cn: gignere「生育、产生」是 genitor 与 generate 的来源。它在拉丁语之前的形式被重构为原始印欧语 *ǵenh₁-，带星号的形式属于重构形式，并非有记录的词。

items.en: Pro- 'forth' plus gignere produced progignere 'bring forth'; its noun progenies named the line of descent rather than a single child.
items.cn: pro-「向前」加 gignere 构成 progignere「向前生出」；其名词 progenies 指一条世系，而非单个孩子。

items.en: Old French progenie carried the noun into English in the fourteenth century; the exact first citation is uncertain.
items.cn: 古法语 progenie 在 14 世纪把这个名词带入英语；确切的最早书证年代不确定。

items.en: By the sixteenth and seventeenth centuries progeny was applied to works, results and successors, not only living offspring.
items.cn: 到 16、17 世纪，progeny 已被用于作品、结果与后继者，不再仅指活着的后代。

items.en: Source uncertain (deeper root): the internal structure of the PIE root is reconstructed, and competing reconstructions exist, so no single form should be treated as settled.
items.cn: 来源不确定（更深词根）：该原始印欧词根的内部结构属于重构，且存在互相竞争的多种重构，因此不应把任何单一形式当作定论。

note.en: Group one holds words that look like progeny or share its root; group two holds the ordinary words for offspring and descendants.
note.cn: 第一组是与 progeny 形近或同根的词；第二组是表示后代与子孙的常用近义词。

entries.tag: same root the one who begets
entries.definition: The agent noun from the same Latin stem: a forefather or precursor, not the offspring itself.
entries.definitionCN: 同一拉丁词干的施事名词：指祖先或先驱，而不是后代本身。

entries.definition: An adjective built on the Latin stem, meaning capable of producing offspring; it describes a capacity, not the young.
entries.definitionCN: 由同一拉丁词干构成的形容词，意为有生育能力；它描述能力，而非幼体。

entries.definition: A rare noun for the act of bringing forth or the offspring produced; it survives mostly in older legal and literary writing.
entries.definitionCN: 罕见名词，指生育行为或所生后代；主要残存于较早的法律与文学文本。

entries.definition: From Latin prodigium 'portent', not from gignere: a marvel or a child of exceptional talent. The resemblance is only in sound.
entries.definitionCN: 来自拉丁 prodigium「预兆」，并非出自 gignere：指奇观或天才儿童。相似仅是读音上的。

entries.definition: The everyday term for the young of a person or animal; it counts individuals more readily than progeny.
entries.definitionCN: 指人或动物幼体的日常通称；比 progeny 更容易逐个计数。

entries.definition: A person or group descended from an ancestor, often used for distant generations rather than the immediate young.
entries.definitionCN: 指某一祖先传下的人或群体，常用于较远的世代而非眼前的幼体。

entries.definition: In law and formal writing, issue means offspring or descendants, especially in wills and genealogies.
entries.definitionCN: 在法律与正式文体中，issue 指后代或子嗣，尤见于遗嘱与族谱。

entries.definition: The whole set of young hatched or born at one time, usually birds; it stresses the group, not the lineage.
entries.definitionCN: 指一次孵化或出生的一整窝幼体，多用于鸟类；强调群体而非世系。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: real morphemes, real collocations and real relatives, not invented rhymes.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的构词成分、真实搭配与真实同族词，而非编造的顺口溜。

normal.en: pro- 'forth' + gignere 'beget': what is brought forth.
normal.cn: pro-「向前」+ gignere「生育」：被生出来之物。

normal.en: The family runs progeny, progenitor, progenitive and progeniture.
normal.cn: 同族词包括 progeny、progenitor、progenitive 与 progeniture。

normal.en: Breeding fixes progeny in the phrase progeny testing.
normal.cn: 畜牧育种把 progeny 固定在后代测验这一短语中。

normal.en: The same Latin stem yields generate, generation and genesis.
normal.cn: 同一拉丁词干还产生 generate、generation 与 genesis。

normal.en: Progeny is a mass noun, so it usually takes a singular verb.
normal.cn: progeny 是集合名词，因此通常接单数动词。

abstract.en: Picture a tree dropping seeds in rings around itself, each ring a generation.
abstract.cn: 想象一棵树在自己周围一圈圈落种，每一圈就是一代。

abstract.en: Picture a book that keeps being rewritten by students who never met the author.
abstract.cn: 想象一本书被从未见过作者的学生不断改写。

abstract.en: Picture a river splitting into channels that all carry the same water.
abstract.cn: 想象一条河分成多股水道，却都带着同样的水。

examples.en: The plant's progeny were replanted on the far side of the valley.
examples.cn: 这株植物的子代被移栽到山谷另一侧。

examples.en: Progeny testing takes years because the offspring must first grow up.
examples.cn: 后代测验需要数年，因为子代必须先长大。

examples.en: His progeny in the profession still cite the same handbook.
examples.cn: 他在这一行里的后继者仍在引用同一本手册。

dict_mnemonic.text: pro（向前）+ gen（生）——向前生出来的一群 → 后代；注意别与 prodigy（奇才、预兆）混。

root: 拉丁 progenies「世系、后代」← pro-（向前）+ gignere（生育）；gignere 与 generate、gene 同出原始印欧语 *ǵenh₁-（重构形式），更深来源不确定。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses follow one gesture: something is brought forth, and that bringing-forth is then read as offspring, lineage, plant young, a product, successors, a breeding test, a collective group and finally a surviving body of work.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项沿同一个动作展开：某物被生出，这一「生出」随后被读作后代、世系、植物子代、产物、后继者、育种测验、集合群体，最后是存续下来的作品整体。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a parent plant sending up a row of seedlings, each carrying part of the same pattern.
core.cn: 核心意象：一株母本植物顶出一排幼苗，每一株都带着同一格局的一部分。

branches.en: LIVING OFFSPRING: animals and plants both bring forth young, and the noun covers either.
branches.cn: 活着的后代：动物与植物都会繁育幼体，这个词两者都覆盖。

branches.en: LINE AND GROUP: the same noun names a chain of generations or one parent's whole brood.
branches.cn: 世系与群体：同一个名词既指代代相连的链，也指某一亲本的整批子代。

branches.en: PRODUCT: an idea or result is pictured as what a cause gives birth to.
branches.cn: 产物：观念或结果被想象成原因所生之物。

branches.en: SUCCESSORS AND WORK: people who carry on a tradition, and the work that outlives its maker.
branches.cn: 后继者与作品：延续传统的人，以及比作者活得更久的作品。

branches.en: BREEDING TEST: the offspring's performance becomes the evidence for judging the parent.
branches.cn: 育种测验：子代表现成为评判亲本的证据。

intro.en: Progeny is a Latin noun whose prefix and root also build several English words, so the family can be read morpheme by morpheme.
intro.cn: progeny 是一个拉丁名词，其前缀与词根还构成若干英语词，因此这个词族可以按语素逐个读出。

latinIntro.en: Latin gignere gives generate, generation, genitor and progeny; pro- adds the sense of bringing something forward.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁 gignere 衍生 generate、generation、genitor 与 progeny；pro- 增添「向前带出」的意思。

items.example: The prefix sends the action outward from a source.
items.exampleCN: 这个前缀把动作从源头往外送出。

items.example: The root names the act of bringing something into being.
items.exampleCN: 这个词根命名「使某物进入存在」的动作。

items.example: Progenies named the whole line rather than one child.
items.exampleCN: progenies 指整条世系，而非单个孩子。

items.example: The mare's progeny were sold at auction.
items.exampleCN: 这匹母马的后代在拍卖会上售出。

items.example: The progenitor of the family arrived in 1700.
items.exampleCN: 这个家族的祖先于 1700 年到来。

items.example: Progenitive cells divide throughout the season.
items.exampleCN: 具生殖能力的细胞在整个季节不断分裂。
反应堆稳定地产生热量。

items.meaning: the act of producing; a cohort
items.example: Each generation inherited the same orchard.
items.exampleCN: 每一代人都继承了同一片果园。

items.structure: Greek genos (same PIE family, not a derivative)
items.example: One gene codes for one product.
items.exampleCN: 一个基因编码一种产物。

items.example: The genesis of the project was a single note.
items.exampleCN: 这个项目起源于一张便条。

latinEntries.structure: gigno, gignere, genui, genitum (verb, third conjugation)

definition_zh: 节目；节目单；计划；方案；（计算机）程序；规划；用程序控制
definition_en: a show or broadcast, a plan of events, a set of instructions for a computer, or the act of arranging such things
core_image: 一页预先写好的清单，把要演出的曲目和要做的事按顺序排在上面
scene: 演出开始前，音乐厅门口的桌上放着一叠薄薄的小册子，观众一边排队一边翻看今晚的曲目。The orchestra printed a slim programme listing every piece for the evening.
sceneCN: 这里取「节目单、节目」的意思（第 1 个义项：广播或演出的节目及其说明）；句意为乐团印了一本薄薄的节目单，列出当晚的每一首曲子。门口那叠小册子就是线索。

pos.zh: 节目；节目单；计划；方案；（计算机）程序

derivatives.zh: 由 programme 加表示「人」的后缀 -er 构成，义为「程序员」
由 programme 去 e 加 -ing 构成，义为「编程；节目编排」
由希腊词干 programmat- 加 -ic 构成，义为「纲领性的；按计划行事的」

senses.title: A show on television or radio
senses.definition: a show broadcast on television or radio, or the printed list of items in a performance
senses.definitionCN: 在电视或广播中播出的节目，也指演出前印好的曲目或环节清单
senses.example: Her cookery programme is shown every Sunday evening.
senses.exampleCN: 她的烹饪节目每周日晚播出。
senses.why: Greek programma was a public written notice, so the word began as something written down and read out before it named what was performed.
senses.whyCN: 希腊语 programma 本指公开写出的通告，所以这个词最初是「写下来给人看的东西」，后来才指被演出或被播出的内容。

senses.title: A plan of events or actions
senses.definition: an organized plan listing the events, steps or work that will be done
senses.definitionCN: 把要做的事件、步骤或工作有条理地列出来的计划
senses.example: The government launched a programme to repair rural roads.
senses.exampleCN: 政府启动了修缮乡村道路的计划。
senses.why: A written notice also fixes an order, so the same word came to mean the ordered list of things to be done.
senses.whyCN: 写出来的通告同时规定了顺序，于是同一个词又指「按顺序排好的待办事项」，也就是计划。

senses.title: A set of instructions for a computer
senses.definition: a series of coded instructions that makes a computer perform a task
senses.definitionCN: 让计算机完成某项任务的一串编码指令
senses.example: He wrote a short programme that sorts the names alphabetically.
senses.exampleCN: 他写了一个短程序，把姓名按字母顺序排序。
senses.why: A computer follows a written sequence step by step, exactly as a theatre follows a printed running order, so the plan sense was reused for machine instructions.
senses.whyCN: 计算机一步步照着写好的顺序执行，就像剧场照着印好的流程单演出，于是「计划」这层意思被挪去指机器指令。

senses.title: To plan or arrange something
senses.definition: to arrange or set out a plan for an event, a machine or a course of action
senses.definitionCN: 为某项活动、某台机器或某个行动方案做出安排
senses.example: The festival was programmed months in advance.
senses.exampleCN: 这个节日的活动提前几个月就安排好了。
senses.why: If a programme is a written order of events, then to programme is to put things into that order, and later to feed that order into a machine.
senses.whyCN: 既然 programme 是写好的事件顺序，那么动词就是「把事情排进这个顺序」，后来也指把顺序输入机器。

intro.en: Programme goes back through French to a Greek word for a public written notice, built from a prefix meaning before and a verb meaning to write.
intro.cn: programme 经法语上溯到一个希腊词，本指公开写出的通告，由表示「在前」的前缀和表示「写」的动词构成。

items.en: The Greek prefix pro- meant before or in front, and graphein meant to write, so the pair described writing something beforehand.
items.cn: 希腊语前缀 pro- 表示「在前」，动词 graphein 表示「写」，两者合起来就是「事先写出」。

items.en: Programma named a public notice put up in advance, such as an official announcement or a posted list.
items.cn: programma 指提前张贴出来的公开通告，例如官方告示或贴出的名单。

items.en: Latin borrowed programma unchanged from Greek and kept the sense of a written public notice.
items.cn: 拉丁语原样借入 programma，仍指写出来的公开通告。

items.en: French programme narrowed the word towards the printed list of a performance and towards a plan of work.
items.cn: 法语 programme 把词义收窄到演出的印刷节目单，以及工作的计划。

items.en: English took the French form as programme, kept it in Britain, and American usage shortened it to program.
items.cn: 英语借入法语形式 programme，英式保留此拼写，美式则简化为 program。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers spellings and relatives built on the same Greek root for writing; the near-meaning group gathers words for shows and plans.
note.cn: 形近组收同一希腊「写」词根上的拼写与同族词；近义组收表示节目与计划的词。

entries.definition: The shorter American spelling, used for shows, plans and computer code.
entries.definitionCN: 较短的美式拼写，同样表示节目、计划与计算机代码。

entries.definition: A person who writes instructions for a computer.
entries.definitionCN: 编写计算机指令的人；程序员。

entries.definition: The work of writing computer code, or of arranging a schedule.
entries.definitionCN: 编写计算机代码的工作，或安排日程的工作。

entries.definition: Planned and organized according to a fixed set of aims.
entries.definitionCN: 按照一套固定目标来计划与组织的；纲领性的。

entries.definition: A performance or broadcast intended to entertain an audience.
entries.definitionCN: 为娱乐观众而演出或播出的内容。

entries.definition: A radio or television transmission.
entries.definitionCN: 广播或电视的播出。

entries.definition: A plan that lists times and events.
entries.definitionCN: 列出时间与事项的计划；日程表。

entries.definition: A large plan, often official, for doing something.
entries.definitionCN: 为做某事而制定的大型计划，常指官方方案。

normalIntro.en: The word began as a written notice, so its memories hang on writing, listing and ordering, and on the machine that now follows such a list.
normalIntro.cn: 这个词本是一份写出来的通告，所以记忆可以挂在「写、列、排序」上，也挂在照着清单执行的机器上。

normal.en: Greek graphein means to write, and English keeps that root in programme, diagram and grammar.
normal.cn: 希腊语 graphein 意为「写」，英语在 programme、diagram、grammar 里都保留了这个词根。

normal.en: The prefix pro- means before, so a programme is literally something written before the event happens.
normal.cn: 前缀 pro- 表示「在前」，所以 programme 字面上就是「活动开始之前写好的东西」。

normal.en: A theatre programme lists items in order and a computer program lists steps in order; the same idea of a written order runs through both.
normal.cn: 剧场节目单按顺序列出节目，计算机程序按顺序列出步骤，两者贯穿的是同一个「写好的顺序」。

normal.en: British English keeps the final -me and the double m, while American English drops them to spell it program.
normal.cn: 英式保留词尾的 me 与双写的 m，美式则省去这些字母，写成 program。

normal.en: Programmer only adds -er to the noun: the person who writes the code.
normal.cn: programmer 只是在名词后加 -er，指写代码的人。

abstract.en: A word that began as a poster and ended as code shows how writing can turn into action.
abstract.cn: 一个从海报变成代码的词，说明写下来的东西可以变成真正的行动。

abstract.en: Every list is a small promise about the future, which is why a show and a plan share one name.
abstract.cn: 每份清单都是对未来的小小承诺，所以一场演出和一份计划共用一个名字。

abstract.en: The machine does not invent the order; it only obeys the order that someone wrote down.
abstract.cn: 机器不会自己发明顺序，它只服从别人写下来的顺序。

examples.en: Her cookery programme is shown every Sunday evening.
examples.cn: 她的烹饪节目每周日晚播出。

examples.en: The city has programmed the traffic lights to favour buses.
examples.cn: 这座城市把交通灯设置成优先放行公交。

examples.en: Our school runs a programme for students who need extra help.
examples.cn: 我们学校为需要额外帮助的学生开办了一个项目。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「普若格拉姆」——听着像「铺个栏目」，把栏目一条条铺开，就是节目单和计划。

root: 希腊语 pro-（在前）+ graphein（写）构成 programma，本指预先写出的公告；经拉丁语 programma 与法语 programme 进入英语，美式拼写简化为 program。

sensesIntro.en: The core is a written list set out in advance; from it grow the show that follows the list, the plan behind it, the machine that executes it, and the act of arranging it.
sensesIntro.cn: 核心是事先写好的一份清单；由它长出照着清单演出的节目、清单背后的计划、执行清单的机器，以及安排清单的动作。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a written sheet pinned up before an event, listing what will happen and in what order.
core.cn: 核心意象：活动开始前贴出的一张纸，写着要发生什么、按什么顺序发生。

branches.en: a printed sheet folded inside a concert hall seat
branches.cn: 音乐厅座椅上折好的印刷节目单

branches.en: a notice board announcing next month's events
branches.cn: 公告板上预告下月活动的通知

branches.en: a minister signing a three-year building plan
branches.cn: 部长签署一份三年建设计划

branches.en: a screen waiting for a line of code to run
branches.cn: 屏幕上等待一行代码运行

branches.en: an engineer slotting steps into the right order
branches.cn: 工程师把各个步骤排进正确的顺序

intro.en: The word rests on a Greek prefix and a Greek verb of writing, then passes through Latin and French before English adds its own endings.
intro.cn: 这个词由希腊语前缀和表示「写」的动词支撑，经拉丁语与法语传入英语，再由英语加上自己的后缀。

latinIntro.en: Latin took programma straight from Greek and used it for a written notice; the same root produced gramma, a written mark or letter.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语直接从希腊语借入 programma，指写出的通告；同一词根还产生 gramma，指写下的符号或字母。

items.meaning: a show, a plan, a set of code

definition_zh: 前进；行进；进步；进展；发展；使前进
definition_en: movement forward, especially towards a goal, or the gradual development and improvement of something
core_image: 一行人沿着山路一步步往上走，身后的路越拉越长
scene: 山路上的人已经走了大半程，回头还能看见来时的弯道。The hikers made slow progress up the ridge before the fog closed in.
sceneCN: 这里取「进展、前进的程度」的意思（第 2 个义项：朝更远或更好的状态发展）；句意为雾合拢之前，徒步者沿着山脊缓慢上行。回头可见的弯道说明他们已经走了很远。

derivatives.zh: 由 progress 加 -ive 构成，义为「渐进的；进步的」
由 progress 加 -ion 构成，义为「进展；序列」
由 progressive 加 -ly 构成，义为「逐渐地」

senses.title: Forward movement towards a place
senses.definition: movement forward, especially of a group of people or a vehicle towards a destination
senses.definitionCN: 向前移动，尤指人群或车辆朝目的地行进
senses.example: The army's progress through the valley was slowed by rain.
senses.exampleCN: 军队穿过山谷的行进被雨拖慢了。
senses.why: Latin progredi is built from pro-, forward, and gradi, to walk, so the first sense is simply walking forward.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 progredi 由 pro-（向前）和 gradi（走）构成，所以最初的意思就是「往前走」。

senses.title: Development towards a better state
senses.definition: the gradual improvement or development of a person, a project or a society
senses.definitionCN: 个人、项目或社会逐渐变好或向前发展
senses.example: She has made real progress in her spoken English.
senses.exampleCN: 她的英语口语有了实实在在的进步。
senses.why: Walking forward easily turns into a metaphor for moving towards a goal, so the word came to mean any step towards something better.
senses.whyCN: 「往前走」很容易被用来比喻「朝目标迈进」，于是这个词就指任何向更好状态靠近的一步。

senses.title: To move forward
senses.definition: to move forward or continue on a course
senses.definitionCN: 向前移动，或沿某条路线继续前行
senses.example: The procession progressed slowly along the narrow street.
senses.exampleCN: 队伍沿着窄街缓慢前行。
senses.why: The verb keeps the literal Latin sense of walking on, and its stress falls on the second syllable, unlike the noun.
senses.whyCN: 动词保留了拉丁语「继续走」的本义，重音落在第二个音节上，与名词不同。

senses.title: To improve or develop
senses.definition: to develop or improve, especially over a period of time
senses.definitionCN: 在一段时间里逐渐发展或变好
senses.example: Work on the new school is progressing faster than expected.
senses.exampleCN: 新学校的工程进展比预期更快。
senses.why: Because the noun already meant improvement, the verb took on the same figurative sense and now often describes projects and conditions.
senses.whyCN: 既然名词已经表示「变好」，动词也就承接了这层比喻义，如今多用来描述工程与状况。

intro.en: Progress comes from a Latin verb that joins forward to walk, and the noun keeps the same image of a journey towards something.
intro.cn: progress 出自一个把「向前」和「走」合起来的拉丁动词，名词里仍保留着「朝某处走」的画面。

items.en: The prefix pro- meant forward, and gradi meant to walk or to step, so the two together described stepping onward.
items.cn: 前缀 pro- 表示向前，动词 gradi 表示走、迈步，两者合起来就是「向前迈」。

items.en: Progredi meant to go forward, to advance, and its past participle progressus supplied the noun.
items.cn: progredi 意为前进、推进，其过去分词 progressus 提供了名词形式。

items.en: Progressus named a going forward, both on the ground and in the course of events.
items.cn: progressus 指向前行进，既指脚下的路，也指事情的进程。

items.en: Old French progres kept the noun sense of advance and passed it into English.
items.cn: 古法语 progres 保留「前进」的名词义，并传入英语。

items.en: Modern English uses progress for movement and improvement, and also as a verb; the noun stresses the first syllable and the verb the second.
items.cn: 现代英语用 progress 表示行进与进步，也可作动词；名词重音在第一音节，动词重音在第二音节。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers words built on the same Latin root of stepping; the near-meaning group gathers words for moving and getting better.
note.cn: 形近组收同一拉丁「迈步」词根上的词；近义组收表示前行与变好的词。

entries.definition: Moving forward step by step, or favouring social reform.
entries.definitionCN: 一步步向前的；主张社会改革的。

entries.definition: A series of steps or stages in a process.
entries.definitionCN: 过程中的一连串步骤或阶段。

entries.definition: To move backwards to an earlier or worse state.
entries.definitionCN: 退回较早或较差的状态。

entries.definition: Happening slowly, in small steps.
entries.definitionCN: 缓慢发生的，一步一步的。

entries.definition: Forward movement, or a step towards a goal.
entries.definitionCN: 向前移动，或朝目标迈出的一步。

entries.definition: The process of growing or becoming more advanced.
entries.definitionCN: 成长或变得更先进的过程。

entries.definition: A change that makes something better.
entries.definitionCN: 使某物变好的改变。

entries.definition: Forward movement, especially against difficulty.
entries.definitionCN: 尤指克服困难后的前进。

normalIntro.en: The word is a walk turned into a picture of improvement, and its family keeps the same forward step.
normalIntro.cn: 这个词把「走路」变成「变好」的比喻，同族词都保留着那一步向前的动作。

normal.en: Latin gradi means to walk, so progress is first a matter of feet, not of grades.
normal.cn: 拉丁语 gradi 意为「走」，所以 progress 最初说的是脚步，而不是分数。

normal.en: The prefix pro- points forward, which is why progress always carries a direction.
normal.cn: 前缀 pro- 指向前方，所以 progress 总带着方向感。

normal.en: The noun puts the beat on the first syllable and the verb on the second, as English often does with such pairs.
normal.cn: 名词重音在第一音节，动词重音在第二音节，英语里这类成对的词常常如此。

normal.en: Progressive adds -ive: a person or policy that keeps moving forward.
normal.cn: progressive 加 -ive，指不断向前的人或政策。

normal.en: Progression adds -ion: the series of steps that a forward movement leaves behind.
normal.cn: progression 加 -ion，指前进过程中留下的一连串步骤。

abstract.en: A journey and an improvement share one word because both are measured by where you were and where you are.
abstract.cn: 旅程和进步共用一个词，因为两者都要靠「原来在哪、现在在哪」来衡量。

abstract.en: Progress is invisible in a single moment; it only appears when you look back at the distance covered.
abstract.cn: 进度在单独一刻里看不见，只有回头看走过的距离时才显现。

abstract.en: The same word can be a thing and an action, which is why English can say that progress progresses.
abstract.cn: 同一个词既能是事物也能是动作，所以英语里可以说 progress 自己在前行。

examples.en: She has made real progress in her spoken English.
examples.cn: 她的英语口语有了实实在在的进步。

examples.en: The procession progressed slowly along the narrow street.
examples.cn: 队伍沿着窄街缓慢前行。

examples.en: Negotiations are still in progress.
examples.cn: 谈判仍在进行中。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「扑若格瑞斯」——听着像「扑过去，格外卖力」，往前一扑再使劲，就是进步。

root: 拉丁语 pro-（向前）+ gradi（走）构成 progredi，过去分词 progressus 意为「向前走」，经古法语 progres 进入英语；名词重音在前，动词重音在后。

sensesIntro.en: The core is walking forward; the senses split into the journey itself, the improvement it stands for, and the two verb uses that follow.
sensesIntro.cn: 核心是「向前走」；义项分成脚下的行进、由它比喻出的进步，以及随之而来的两种动词用法。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a group of walkers moving steadily along a ridge, with the ground already covered stretching out behind them.
core.cn: 核心意象：一队人沿着山脊稳步向前，走过的路在身后越拉越长。

branches.en: a column of walkers rounding a bend
branches.cn: 一队行人绕过弯道

branches.en: a learner reading a page that once looked impossible
branches.cn: 学习者读着一页曾经觉得很难读的文字

branches.en: a river of people moving through a narrow street
branches.cn: 人流沿着窄街向前移动

branches.en: a building site gaining a floor each month
branches.cn: 工地每个月多出一层

branches.en: a project that is visibly further along than last year
branches.cn: 比去年明显推进了的项目

intro.en: The word is built from a Latin prefix of forward movement and a Latin verb of walking, with English endings added later.
intro.cn: 这个词由表示向前的拉丁语前缀和表示行走的拉丁语动词构成，英语后缀是后来加上的。

latinIntro.en: Latin gradi, to walk, and its participle progressus sit behind the English noun and verb.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 gradi（走）及其分词 progressus 是英语名词与动词的来源。

definition_zh: 进展；进程；序列；级数
definition_en: the process of moving forward step by step, or an ordered sequence of stages, numbers or chords
core_image: 一排台阶向远处升高，每一级上都刻着下一个数字
scene: 这里指「进展」。 The progression from trainee to manager took eight years.
sceneCN: 这里 progression 是「进程、逐步发展」（第 1 个义项：一级一级向前推进）；句意：从实习生到经理的进程用了八年。图中可辨识物件：逐级升高的台阶、台阶上的数字、远处的台阶尽端。

senses.title: Forward movement in steps
senses.definition: the act of moving forward through a series of stages
senses.definitionCN: 通过一系列阶段向前推进的行为
senses.example: The progression from symptom to diagnosis was slow.
senses.exampleCN: 从出现症状到确诊的进程很慢。
senses.why: pro- 'forward' plus gradi 'to walk' gives progredi, 'to go forward'. The noun names a walking forward that happens in steps.
senses.whyCN: pro-“向前”加 gradi“行走”构成 progredi“前行”。名词命名一步一步向前走的动作。

senses.title: An ordered sequence
senses.definition: the order in which things follow one another, considered apart from the movement
senses.definitionCN: 事物相互接续的次序，被视为独立于移动过程
senses.example: The chapters form a clear progression of ideas.
senses.exampleCN: 这些章节构成清晰的思想序列。
senses.why: Once steps are numbered, the word can name the ladder instead of the climbing.
senses.whyCN: 一旦给台阶编号，这个词就可命名梯子本身，而不是攀爬。

senses.title: Gradual development
senses.titleCN: 逐步发展：慢慢变成另一个样子
senses.definition: a series of small changes that add up to a larger transformation
senses.definitionCN: 一系列小变化累积成较大转变
senses.example: The city's progression from port to financial centre took a century.
senses.exampleCN: 这座城市从港口发展为金融中心用了一个世纪。
senses.why: Gradual change is progress measured in small gradi, each step small enough to be unremarkable alone.
senses.whyCN: 渐变是以细小步伐衡量的前进，每一步单独看都不起眼。

senses.title: Mathematics: a progression
senses.definition: a sequence of numbers in which each term follows the previous by a fixed rule, as in arithmetic or geometric progression
senses.definitionCN: 按固定规则由前一项得到后一项的数列，如等差或等比数列
senses.example: The terms form an arithmetic progression with a difference of three.
senses.exampleCN: 这些项构成公差为三的等差数列。
senses.why: Mathematics abstracts the staircase into numbers: each step adds or multiplies by the same amount.
senses.whyCN: 数学把台阶抽象成数字：每一步加或乘同一个量。

senses.title: Music: chord progression
senses.definition: the sequence of chords through which a piece moves
senses.definitionCN: 一首乐曲依次经过的和弦序列
senses.example: The song uses a simple four-chord progression.
senses.exampleCN: 这首歌用了简单的四和弦进行。
senses.why: Harmony moves in steps too, so musicians borrowed the walking word for the order of chords.
senses.whyCN: 和声也按步移动，所以音乐家借用了“行走”的词来指和弦次序。

senses.title: Clinical progression
senses.definition: in medicine, the way a disease develops or worsens over time
senses.definitionCN: 医学上指疾病随时间发展或加重的过程
senses.example: The scan shows progression of the lesion.
senses.exampleCN: 扫描显示病灶有进展。
senses.why: Clinical use is directional but not positive: progression here can mean getting worse, which shows the word names movement, not improvement.
senses.whyCN: 临床用法有方向但不含正面意义：这里进展可以指恶化，说明这个词命名移动，而非改善。

senses.title: Career progression
senses.titleCN: 职业晋升：一级一级上去
senses.definition: the movement from one job level or role to a higher one
senses.definitionCN: 从一个职位层级或角色向更高层级移动
senses.example: The company publishes a clear career progression path.
senses.exampleCN: 公司公布了一条清晰的职业晋升路径。
senses.why: Workplaces turn the staircase into job grades, so progression becomes a synonym for promotion over time.
senses.whyCN: 职场把台阶变成职级，因此 progression 成为随时间晋升的同义词。

senses.title: Logical progression
senses.definition: the order in which an argument or narrative moves from one point to the next
senses.definitionCN: 论证或叙述从一个要点推进到下一个要点的次序
senses.example: The essay lacks a logical progression between paragraphs.
senses.exampleCN: 这篇文章段落之间缺少逻辑递进。
senses.why: Reasoning also walks: each claim should stand on the one before, which is why writers speak of a progression of ideas.
senses.whyCN: 推理也在行走：每个主张应站在前一个之上，所以写作者说“思想递进”。

intro.en: Progression comes from Latin progressio 'a going forward', from progredi 'to go forward', built on pro- 'forward' plus gradi 'to walk, step'.
intro.cn: progression 来自拉丁 progressio“向前行走”，源于 progredi“前行”，由 pro-“向前”加 gradi“行走、迈步”构成。

items.en: gradi meant 'to walk, step, go'. Its noun gradus 'step' gives grade, gradual and degree, so the family is built on the single step.
items.cn: gradi 意为“行走、迈步、前进”。其名词 gradus“步”产出 grade、gradual、degree，整个词族都建立在“一步”上。

items.en: pro- 'forward' plus gradi gives progredi, 'to go forward'. The prefix fixes direction; the verb supplies the walking.
items.cn: pro-“向前”加 gradi 构成 progredi“前行”。前缀固定方向，动词提供“走”。

items.en: The action noun progressio named a going forward, and could also mean a literary or logical advance.
items.cn: 动作名词 progressio 指向前行进，也可指文辞或论证上的推进。

items.en: English borrows progression through French, first for physical advance and then for the order of events.
items.cn: 英语经法语借入 progression，先指物理前进，后指事件次序。

items.en: In the 17th century mathematics fixes arithmetic and geometric progression as names for number sequences.
items.cn: 17 世纪数学固定了等差数列与等比数列作为数列的名称。

items.en: Later centuries add clinical progression and chord progression, extending the staircase to disease and harmony.
items.cn: 此后几个世纪加入病程进展与和弦进行，把台阶扩展到疾病与和声。

note.en: The look-alike group shares the grad- stem or the pro- prefix; the near-meaning group all involve moving forward, differing in pace and direction.
note.cn: 形近组共享 grad- 词干或 pro- 前缀；近义组都涉及向前，差别在速度与方向。

entries.tag: same root verb or mass noun
entries.definition: forward movement or improvement, usually uncountable. Progression stresses the step-by-step series.
entries.definitionCN: 前进；进步，通常不可数。progression 强调一步一步的序列。

entries.definition: happening gradually, or favoring reform. The adjective describes the manner or the politics.
entries.definitionCN: 渐进的；进步的。形容词描述方式或政治立场。

entries.definition: hostile or forceful. It comes from ad- 'toward' plus gradi, 'to step toward', and has nothing to do with progress.
entries.definitionCN: 攻击性的。来自 ad-“朝向”加 gradi“迈步”，与 progress 无关。

entries.definition: a set of things in a fixed order. It names the arrangement, while progression can name the moving through it.
entries.definitionCN: 序列。它命名排列，而 progression 可命名在其中推进的过程。

entries.definition: the process of growing or becoming more advanced. It stresses change in quality, not ordered steps.
entries.definitionCN: 发展。强调性质变化，不强调有序步骤。

entries.definition: a single movement forward or an improvement. It is one step, while progression is the series of steps.
entries.definitionCN: 前进；进展。它是一步，而 progression 是一系列步。

entries.definition: movement backward or return to an earlier state. It is the direct opposite of progression.
entries.definitionCN: 倒退；回归。它是 progression 的直接反面。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: real morphemes, real collocations and real relatives, not invented rhymes.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的构词成分、真实搭配与真实同族词。

normal.en: gradi 'walk' is the core, so a progression is a walk with numbered steps.
normal.cn: gradi“行走”是核心，所以 progression 是一次给每一步编号的行走。

normal.en: grade, gradual and degree all come from gradus 'step', which makes the staircase image easy to keep.
normal.cn: grade、gradual、degree 都出自 gradus“步”，台阶意象很好记。

normal.en: Arithmetic progression and geometric progression show the rule: add a constant or multiply by one.
normal.cn: 等差数列与等比数列显示规则：加一个常数，或乘一个常数。

normal.en: Chord progression is harmony walking from one chord to the next.
normal.cn: 和弦进行就是和声从一个和弦走到下一个。

normal.en: Clinical progression can mean getting worse, which proves the word is about movement, not improvement.
normal.cn: 病程进展可以指恶化，证明这个词关乎移动，而非改善。

abstract.en: Picture a staircase where each step is numbered one higher.
abstract.cn: 想象一级级台阶，每级数字比前一级大一。

abstract.en: Picture a film shown frame by frame rather than all at once.
abstract.cn: 想象一部电影逐帧播放，而不是一次全放。

abstract.en: Picture a path of stepping stones that only makes sense from the first stone onward.
abstract.cn: 想象一条踏石小径，只有从第一块石起才看得懂。

examples.en: The progression of the illness was faster than expected.
examples.cn: 病情进展比预期更快。

examples.en: Each term in the progression is double the one before.
examples.cn: 这个数列中每一项都是前一项的两倍。

examples.en: Her career progression followed a steady path through three departments.
examples.cn: 她的职业晋升沿着一条稳定路径，跨过三个部门。

dict_mnemonic.text: “普若格瑞神”音近 progression：一步一步“格”上去、像有“神”力推着走——逐级向前 → progression 进程

root: 拉丁 pro-“向前”+ gradi“行走”（名词 gradus“步”）→ progredi“前行”→ progressio；英语取 progression 词干 + -ion。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses all describe movement or order in steps, whether the steps are stages, numbers, chords or arguments.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项都描述“按步移动或按步排列”，无论步是阶段、数字、和弦还是论证。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: numbered steps climbing into the distance.
core.cn: 核心意象：一级级带编号的台阶伸向远方。

branches.en: WALK AND LADDER: the moving and the order are the verb side and the structure side of one image.
branches.cn: 行走与梯子：移动与次序是同一意象的动词面与结构面。

branches.en: GRADUAL CHANGE: many small steps add up to a new state.
branches.cn: 渐变：许多小步累积成新状态。

branches.en: RULES OF ORDER: numbers and chords both advance by a fixed rule.
branches.cn: 次序规则：数字与和弦都按固定规则推进。

branches.en: CLINICAL DIRECTION: progression can be worsening, which shows the word is neutral about value.
branches.cn: 临床方向：进展可以指恶化，说明这个词对价值是中性的。

branches.en: SOCIAL AND LOGICAL LADDERS: job grades and argument steps are both ordered climbing.
branches.cn: 社会与逻辑阶梯：职级与论证步骤都是有序攀爬。

intro.en: Progression is pro- plus gradi plus -ion. The prefix marks direction, the verb marks walking, and the suffix makes the series a noun.
intro.cn: progression 由 pro- 加 gradi 加 -ion 构成。前缀标记方向，动词标记行走，后缀把序列变成名词。

latinIntro.en: Latin gradi 'walk' → progredi 'go forward' → progressio. The same gradi gives grade, gradual, ingredient and aggressive.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁 gradi“行走”→ progredi“前行”→ progressio。同一 gradi 还产出 grade、gradual、ingredient、aggressive。

definition_zh: 禁止；阻止；使不可能；（法律）禁止某人做某事
definition_en: to forbid something by law or rule, or to make it impossible
core_image: 一只手横在门前，掌心朝外，把来人挡回去
scene: 博物馆入口挂着一块牌子。The sign at the entrance says that the rules prohibit flash photography, and the guard raises a hand whenever a camera comes up.
sceneCN: 这里 prohibit 是「禁止」（第 1 个义项：以规则明令不许做某事）；句意：入口的牌子写着规定禁止使用闪光灯，保安一看到有人举相机就抬手示意。图中可辨识物件：禁止标识、相机、闪光灯、保安的手、展厅入口；对应第 1 个义项。

derivatives.zh: 禁止的；（价格）高得使人却步的

senses.title: Forbid by law or rule
senses.definition: to state officially that something must not be done
senses.definitionCN: 官方规定某事不得做
senses.example: The law prohibits smoking indoors.
senses.exampleCN: 法律禁止室内吸烟。
senses.why: Latin prohibere means 'hold back'. The prefix pro- pushes away, and habere holds: the rule puts a hand out and holds the thing back from happening.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 prohibere 意为“挡住”。前缀 pro- 向外推，habere 是持握：规则伸出一只手，把此事挡在外面。

senses.title: Prevent or make impossible
senses.definition: to make something impossible in practice
senses.definitionCN: 使某事在实践中不可能
senses.example: The high cost prohibits most families from buying.
senses.exampleCN: 高昂的成本使多数家庭无法购买。
senses.why: The same holding-back can be economic rather than legal: price acts like a gate. Prohibitive costs prohibit without any statute.
senses.whyCN: 同一种“挡住”可以是经济的而非法律的：价格像一道门。 prohibitive 的成本无需法规就禁止了购买。

senses.title: Forbid a person from doing
senses.definition: to bar a specific person from an action
senses.definitionCN: 禁止特定的人采取某行动
senses.example: The court prohibited him from contacting her.
senses.exampleCN: 法庭禁止他联系她。
senses.why: When the object is a person, the rule targets an agent rather than an act. The structure prohibit someone from doing marks the boundary drawn around that person.
senses.whyCN: 当对象是人时，规则瞄准行动者而非行为本身。prohibit someone from doing 的结构，标记围绕此人画下的边界。

senses.title: An official ban
senses.definition: to ban something officially, often by authority
senses.definitionCN: 由权威正式取缔某物
senses.example: The city prohibited the sale of fireworks.
senses.exampleCN: 该市禁止销售烟花爆竹。
senses.why: A ban is the institutional form of the hand at the door. Prohibition is the noun, and it can name a whole historical policy, as in the American Prohibition.
senses.whyCN: 禁令是“门口那只手”的制度形式。prohibition 是名词，可以命名一整段历史政策，如美国禁酒令。

senses.title: Of a sign or notice: forbid entry or use
senses.definition: of a sign or instruction, to forbid an action or access
senses.definitionCN: 标识或指示禁止某行为或进入
senses.example: The sign prohibits entry without a badge.
senses.exampleCN: 标牌禁止无证进入。
senses.why: Public space is regulated by visible marks. The verb turns a printed symbol into a rule, and the sign becomes the hand made permanent.
senses.whyCN: 公共空间由可见标记管理。动词把印刷符号变成规则，标牌成了被永久化的那只手。

senses.title: Hinder or prevent (archaic)
senses.definition: in older usage, to hinder or stand in the way of
senses.definitionCN: 旧用法：妨碍或挡路
senses.example: Bad weather prohibited our advance.
senses.exampleCN: 恶劣天气阻碍了我们前进。
senses.why: This is the broadest layer: anything that holds you back prohibits you. Modern English narrows the word to rules and practical impossibility.
senses.whyCN: 这是最宽的一层：任何挡住你的东西都 prohibit 你。现代英语把这个词收窄到规则与实际不可能。

senses.title: Restrain by legal writ
senses.definition: in law, to restrain an action by authority
senses.definitionCN: 法律中以权威限制某行为
senses.example: The injunction prohibits further construction.
senses.exampleCN: 禁令限制继续施工。
senses.why: Courts issue orders that function as verbal gates. The legal sense specializes the holding-back into a formal instrument with penalties attached.
senses.whyCN: 法院发布命令，功能如同语言的门。法律义把“挡住”专门化为附有惩罚的正式工具。

senses.title: Forbid access
senses.definition: to bar entry to a place
senses.definitionCN: 不许进入某地
senses.example: The area is prohibited to civilians.
senses.exampleCN: 该区域禁止平民进入。
senses.why: Access control is the most physical version: a fence, a guard, a sign. The verb names the rule that the barrier enforces.
senses.whyCN: 出入控制是最物理的版本：围栏、警卫、标牌。动词命名屏障所执行的规则。

intro.en: Prohibit is a holding-back word. Latin prohibere joins pro- 'away' to habere 'hold': to hold something away from you, and therefore to forbid it.
intro.cn: prohibit 是一个“挡住”的词。拉丁语 prohibere 把 pro-“向外”与 habere“持握”结合：把某物挡在你之外，因此就是禁止它。

items.en: First recorded as 'forbid, prevent', borrowed from Latin prohibitus.
items.cn: 最早记录为“禁止、阻止”，借自拉丁语 prohibitus。

items.en: prohibitus is the past participle of prohibere 'hold back, keep off, prevent, forbid' = pro- 'away, forth' + habere 'to hold'.
items.cn: prohibitus 是 prohibere 的过去分词，后者意为“挡住、隔开、阻止、禁止”= pro-“向外”+ habere“持握”。

items.en: habere also gives habit, exhibit, inhibit, and ability. The family is about holding, and pro- turns holding into holding away.
items.cn: habere 还生成 habit、exhibit、inhibit、ability。这个词族关乎持握，而 pro- 把“持握”变成“挡开”。

items.en: The noun prohibition and the adjective prohibitive develop, the latter also taking the sense 'so costly as to prevent'.
items.cn: 名词 prohibition 与形容词 prohibitive 发展出来，后者还取得“贵到使人却步”的义。

items.en: Modern English uses prohibit for legal bans, signs, and practical impossibility, keeping the image of a hand held out.
items.cn: 现代英语用 prohibit 指法律禁令、标识与实际不可能，保留“伸出手挡住”的意象。

note.en: The first group shares the habere root; the second is about verbs that also mean forbidding or preventing.
note.cn: 第一组共享 habere 词根，第二组看同样表示“禁止”或“阻止”的动词。

entries.definition: to restrain or slow down. It uses in- 'in' + habere, holding in.
entries.definitionCN: 抑制；阻碍。它用 in-“在内”+ habere，持握在内。

entries.definition: to show publicly. It is ex- 'out' + habere, holding out.
entries.definitionCN: 公开展示。它是 ex-“向外”+ habere，持出在外。

entries.definition: an official ban, or the historical US ban on alcohol.
entries.definitionCN: 官方禁令；美国禁酒令。

entries.definition: to order someone not to do something. It is broader and more personal than prohibit.
entries.definitionCN: 命令某人不要做。它比 prohibit 更宽、更对人。

entries.definition: to forbid something officially, often by public authority. It is the plain word behind prohibition.
entries.definitionCN: 官方禁止，常由公共权威发布。它是 prohibition 背后的平实词。

entries.definition: to stop something from happening. It covers both rules and practical obstacles.
entries.definitionCN: 阻止某事发生。它涵盖规则与实际障碍。

normalIntro.en: Real links: Latin habere 'hold' with pro- 'away', the inhibit/exhibit family, the sign use, and prohibitive cost.
normalIntro.cn: 真实联系：拉丁语 habere“持握”加 pro-“向外”、inhibit/exhibit 词族、标识用法，以及 prohibitive cost。

normal.en: Habere means 'hold'; pro- means 'away'. Prohibit is to hold something away from you: a hand at the door.
normal.cn: habere 意为“持握”；pro- 意为“向外”。prohibit 就是把东西挡在你之外：门口的一只手。

normal.en: Inhibit holds in, exhibit holds out, prohibit holds away: the prefix tells you the direction.
normal.cn: inhibit 向内持，exhibit 向外持，prohibit 挡开：前缀告诉你方向。

normal.en: A prohibition sign is the hand made permanent: the rule stays at the door even when no guard is there.
normal.cn: 禁止标识是被永久化的那只手：即使没有警卫，规则仍守在门口。

normal.en: Prohibitive costs prohibit without a law: price acts as a gate.
normal.cn: prohibitive 的成本无需法律就禁止：价格就是门。

normal.en: The word targets both acts and people: you prohibit smoking, and you prohibit someone from smoking.
normal.cn: 这个词既针对行为也针对人：prohibit smoking，也 prohibit someone from smoking。

abstract.en: Every prohibition draws a boundary, and every boundary creates a category of the forbidden.
abstract.cn: 每一项禁令都画出一条边界，每条边界都造出“被禁止者”这一类别。

abstract.en: Forbidding is cheaper than preventing: a rule costs words, a wall costs stone.
abstract.cn: 禁止比阻止便宜：规则花的是话，墙花的是石头。

abstract.en: The same verb covers law and economics, which shows that constraint has many currencies.
abstract.cn: 同一个动词覆盖法律与经济，说明约束有多种货币。

examples.en: Smoking is prohibited in all public buildings.
examples.cn: 所有公共建筑内禁止吸烟。

examples.en: The high price prohibits many students from applying.
examples.cn: 高昂的价格使许多学生无法申请。

examples.en: The court prohibited the company from selling the drug.
examples.cn: 法庭禁止该公司销售这种药物。

dict_mnemonic.text: “扑若黑壁”——扑到黑色的墙壁前被挡住 → prohibit 禁止、阻止

root: 拉丁语 prohibere“挡住、禁止”= pro-“向外”+ habere“持握”；同族有 habit、exhibit、inhibit、ability。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses of prohibit, all one gesture: holding something away. The hand can be a law, a sign, a court order, a price, or a fence.
sensesIntro.cn: prohibit 的八个义项，都是同一个手势：把某物挡在外面。这只手可以是法律、标识、法院命令、价格或围栏。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a hand held out to keep something away.
core.cn: 核心意象：伸出一只手，把某物挡在外面。

branches.en: RULE: laws, bans, and signs state what must not be done.
branches.cn: 规则：法律、禁令与标识规定什么不得做。

branches.en: PERSON AND COURT: an order can be drawn around a specific person or action.
branches.cn: 人与法庭：命令可围绕特定人或行为画界。

branches.en: ACCESS: a barrier enforces the rule at a physical threshold.
branches.cn: 进入：屏障在物理门槛上执行规则。

branches.en: ECONOMICS: price holds people back without any statute.
branches.cn: 经济：价格无需法规就把人挡住。

branches.en: HINDRANCE: the archaic sense covers any obstacle that holds you back.
branches.cn: 妨碍：古义涵盖任何挡住你的障碍。

intro.en: Prohibit is a Latin verb. English adds -ion, -ive, and -ed, and the root habere also builds inhibit, exhibit, and habit.
intro.cn: prohibit 是拉丁动词。英语加 -ion、-ive、-ed，词根 habere 还构成 inhibit、exhibit、habit。

latinIntro.en: Latin prohibere 'hold back' combines pro- 'away' with habere 'hold'. The same habere underlies exhibit (hold out), inhibit (hold in), and habit (what one holds).
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 prohibere“挡住”把 pro-“向外”与 habere“持握”结合。同一个 habere 支撑 exhibit（持出）、inhibit（持内）与 habit（所持之物）。

items.meaning: an official ban; the act of forbidding
forbidding; so costly as to prevent use
items.meaningCN: 禁止性的；贵得使人却步的

items.meaning: a settled practice; a customary way

latinEntries.meaning: to hold back, keep off, forbid

definition_zh: 项目；工程；课题；计划；投射；凸出；预测；表现（形象）
definition_en: a planned piece of work, or to throw something forward in space, time, or imagination
core_image: 把一张纸向前抛出去，纸面在空中展开成一块可见的平面
scene: 会议室里，团队把目标、时间线、负责人写在墙上。The whole project is pinned to the wall, with its goals, its timeline and the name of the person who owns each part.
sceneCN: 这里 project 是「项目、工程」（第 1 个义项：为达成目标而规划的一整块工作）；句意：整个项目都贴在墙上，写着目标、时间线，以及每一部分的负责人。图中可辨识物件：项目看板、便利贴、时间线、负责人照片、马克笔；对应第 1 个义项。

pos.zh: 投射；凸出；预测；表现（形象）；使（影像）成像

senses.title: A planned piece of work
senses.definition: a planned undertaking with a goal, a timetable, and resources
senses.definitionCN: 有计划、有目标、有时间与资源的任务
senses.example: The bridge project will take five years.
senses.exampleCN: 这座桥的工程要五年。
senses.why: Latin proiectum is 'something thrown forward'. A project is a plan thrown ahead of you, a future state you have already sketched.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 proiectum 是“被抛向前之物”。project 是被投到你前方的计划，一幅你已勾画出的未来图景。

senses.title: A research or study topic
senses.definition: a specific piece of research or academic work
senses.definitionCN: 一项具体的研究或学术工作
senses.example: She is working on a project about urban birds.
senses.exampleCN: 她在做一个关于城市鸟类的课题。
senses.why: Schools and labs cut knowledge into manageable pieces. Each project is a bounded task with its own question, method, and deadline.
senses.whyCN: 学校与实验室把知识切成可处理的块。每个 project 都是有界任务，有自己的问题、方法与期限。

senses.title: To estimate or forecast
senses.definition: to calculate what a quantity will be in the future
senses.definitionCN: 计算某数量在未来会是多少
senses.example: Analysts project a rise in demand.
senses.exampleCN: 分析师预计需求上升。
senses.why: Forecasting is throwing a number forward in time. The same verb that launches an object through space launches a figure into next year.
senses.whyCN: 预测是把一个数字抛向未来。同一个把物体抛过空间的动词，也把数字抛进明年。

senses.title: To throw forward physically
senses.definition: to throw or cast something forward
senses.definitionCN: 把某物向前抛
senses.example: The machine projects balls at high speed.
senses.exampleCN: 这台机器高速抛出球。
senses.why: This is the literal core: iacere 'to throw' with pro- 'forward'. Every abstract sense is a metaphor built on this physical cast.
senses.whyCN: 这是字面核心：iacere“投”加 pro-“向前”。一切抽象义都建在这个物理抛掷上。

senses.title: To cast an image onto a surface
senses.definition: to cause light or an image to fall on a surface
senses.definitionCN: 使光或影像落在某个表面
senses.example: The device projects the map onto the wall.
senses.exampleCN: 设备把地图投射到墙上。
senses.why: Light is thrown forward and lands on a screen. The projector is the object that throws, and the image is what arrives.
senses.whyCN: 光被抛向前方，落在屏幕上。projector 是抛掷之物，影像则是到达之物。

senses.title: To extend outward
senses.definition: of a part, to stick out beyond the main body
senses.definitionCN: 某部分超出主体向外伸
senses.example: The balcony projects over the street.
senses.exampleCN: 阳台向街道上方凸出。
senses.why: A shape that juts out is literally thrown beyond the wall. Architecture uses the word for any part that advances past its base.
senses.whyCN: 向外突出的形状，字面上被抛出了墙外。建筑学用这个词指任何越过基线的部分。

senses.title: To convey an impression
senses.definition: to communicate a quality or image to others
senses.definitionCN: 向他人传达某种品质或形象
senses.example: A good speaker projects confidence.
senses.exampleCN: 好的演讲者展现自信。
senses.why: Social presence is treated as a projection: an inner state is thrown outward so others can see it. The word implies deliberate display.
senses.whyCN: 社会在场被当作一种投射：内在状态被抛到外面，让他人看见。这个词隐含刻意的展示。

senses.title: To predict by extrapolation
senses.definition: to extend a trend or pattern into the future
senses.definitionCN: 把趋势或模式延伸到未来
senses.example: The model projects growth through 2030.
senses.exampleCN: 模型推算增长将持续到 2030 年。
senses.why: Statistics throws a line forward from known points. Projection is the noun, and it always carries the caveat that the future may not land where the line points.
senses.whyCN: 统计把一条线从已知点向前抛。projection 是名词，且总带着警告：未来未必落在线的落点。

senses.title: To protrude anatomically
senses.definition: of a body part, to stick out from the surface
senses.definitionCN: 身体某部分从表面突出
senses.example: The jaw projects forward.
senses.exampleCN: 下颌向前突出。
senses.why: Bones and features can be thrown beyond the body's outline. Anatomy uses the same spatial verb as architecture, applied to flesh.
senses.whyCN: 骨与特征可以超出身体轮廓。解剖学把与建筑相同的空间动词用于肉体。

senses.title: To map onto a plane (geometry)
senses.definition: to represent a figure on a plane by drawing lines from it
senses.definitionCN: 用射线把图形表示到平面上
senses.example: Project the sphere onto a flat map.
senses.exampleCN: 把球面投影到平面地图上。
senses.why: Geometry formalizes the light image: points are carried along rays to a surface. Map projections keep the same metaphor, with distortion as the price.
senses.whyCN: 几何学把光的意象形式化：点沿射线被带到表面。地图投影保留同一隐喻，代价是变形。

intro.en: Project is a throwing word. Latin proicere joins pro- 'forward' to iacere 'to throw'. A plan, an image, a forecast, and a balcony are all things thrown ahead of the body.
intro.cn: project 是一个抛掷词。拉丁语 proicere 把 pro-“向前”与 iacere“投”结合。计划、影像、预测与阳台，都是被抛到身体前方的东西。

items.en: The noun is first recorded as 'a plan, scheme, design'.
items.cn: 名词最早记录为“计划、方案、设计”。

items.en: From Latin proiectum 'something thrown forth', neuter past participle of proicere 'throw forward' = pro- 'forward' + iacere 'to throw'.
items.cn: 来自拉丁语 proiectum“被抛向前之物”，是 proicere“向前抛”的中性过去分词 = pro-“向前”+ iacere“投”。

items.en: iacere also gives eject, inject, reject, subject, and object. The family is about throwing, and the prefix sets the direction.
items.cn: iacere 还生成 eject、inject、reject、subject、object。这个词族关乎投掷，前缀定方向。

items.en: The verb appears with the sense 'to throw or cast forward'.
items.cn: 动词出现，义为“向前投掷”。

items.en: Projection extends to optics, psychology (projecting an image), and statistics (projecting a trend).
items.cn: projection 扩展到光学、心理学（投射形象）与统计学（推算趋势）。

items.en: Modern English uses project for both a planned task and the act of throwing an image, a forecast, or a shape forward.
items.cn: 现代英语用 project 既指计划任务，也指把影像、预测或形状向前抛出的动作。

note.en: The first group shares the iacere root and the -ject shape; the second is about words that also mean a plan or a forecast.
note.cn: 第一组共享 iacere 词根与 -ject 形态，第二组看同样表示“计划”或“预测”的词。

entries.definition: the act of projecting; a forecast or a protruding part.
entries.definitionCN: 投射；预测；凸出部分。

entries.definition: a device that throws an image onto a surface.
entries.definitionCN: 把影像投到表面的设备。

entries.definition: to throw back; to refuse. It is re- 'back' + iacere.
entries.definitionCN: 掷回；拒绝。它是 re-“向后”+ iacere。

entries.definition: a detailed proposal for doing something. It emphasizes intention, not the work itself.
entries.definitionCN: 做某事的详细提议。它强调意图，而非工作本身。

entries.definition: a statement about what will happen. It matches project sense 3 but is more concrete.
entries.definitionCN: 关于将发生之事的陈述。它对应 project 第 3 义，但更具体。

entries.definition: a risky new business or activity. It stresses risk rather than planning.
entries.definitionCN: 有风险的新事业。它强调风险，而非规划。

normalIntro.en: Real links: Latin iacere 'throw', the pro- 'forward' prefix, the reject/inject/eject family, and the optics and statistics uses.
normalIntro.cn: 真实联系：拉丁语 iacere“投”、前缀 pro-“向前”、reject/inject/eject 词族，以及光学与统计用法。

normal.en: Iacere means 'throw'; pro- means 'forward'. A project is something thrown ahead of you.
normal.cn: iacere 意为“投”；pro- 意为“向前”。project 是被抛到你前方的东西。

normal.en: Reject throws back, inject throws in, eject throws out, project throws forward: the prefix is the direction.
normal.cn: reject 掷回，inject 掷入，eject 掷出，project 掷向前：前缀就是方向。

normal.en: A projector throws light; a balcony throws itself beyond the wall; a forecast throws a number into next year.
normal.cn: 投影仪抛光；阳台把自己抛出墙外；预测把数字抛进明年。

normal.en: Project management is planning seen as a launched object: it has a target, a trajectory, and a landing date.
normal.cn: 项目管理就是把计划看作被发射的物体：它有目标、弹道与落地日期。

normal.en: Projecting confidence is throwing an inner state outward so others can catch it.
normal.cn: 展现自信，是把内在状态抛到外面，让他人接住。

abstract.en: Planning is projective: to make a project is to live in a future you have already thrown into view.
abstract.cn: 规划是投射性的：做一个项目，就是住在一个已被你抛入视野的未来里。

abstract.en: Every projection distorts: a map, a forecast, and a self-image all flatten something three-dimensional.
abstract.cn: 每一种投影都会变形：地图、预测与自我形象，都把某种立体之物压平。

abstract.en: The word ties action to imagination: what we throw forward is first an object of thought, then a thing in the world.
abstract.cn: 这个词把行动与想象绑在一起：我们抛向前方的，先是思想的对象，然后才是世界中的实物。

examples.en: The team finished the project ahead of schedule.
examples.cn: 团队提前完成了项目。

examples.en: The film was projected onto a huge screen.
examples.cn: 影片被投射到一块巨大的屏幕上。

examples.en: Sales are projected to grow by ten percent.
examples.cn: 销售额预计增长百分之十。

dict_mnemonic.text: “扑若杰克特”——扑向前，像杰克特（飞镖）一样被抛出 → project 项目、投射

root: 拉丁语 proicere“向前抛”= pro-“向前”+ iacere“投”；过去分词 proiectum。同族有 eject、inject、reject、subject。

sensesIntro.en: Ten senses of project, all one throw. What is thrown can be a plan (a project), an image (a projection), a number (a forecast), a wall (a balcony), or a self (a persona).
sensesIntro.cn: project 的十个义项，都是同一次抛掷。被抛出的可以是计划（项目）、影像（投影）、数字（预测）、墙体（阳台），或自我（形象）。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: something thrown forward from the body into space or time.
core.cn: 核心意象：某物从身体被抛向前方，进入空间或时间。

branches.en: PLAN: a future task sketched and thrown ahead.
branches.cn: 计划：被勾画并抛向前方的未来任务。

branches.en: CAST: physical throwing, light onto a surface, and geometric projection.
branches.cn: 投射：物理抛掷、光落表面与几何投影。

branches.en: PROTRUDE: a part thrown beyond the outline, in buildings and bodies.
branches.cn: 凸出：在建筑与身体中超出轮廓的部分。

branches.en: PERSONA: an inner state thrown outward for others to see.
branches.cn: 形象：内在状态被抛向外，供他人看见。

branches.en: FORECAST: a number or trend carried into the future.
branches.cn: 预测：被带到未来的数字或趋势。

intro.en: Project is noun and verb. English adds -ion, -or, and -ed, and the root iacere also builds reject, inject, eject, and subject.
intro.cn: project 既是名词也是动词。英语加 -ion、-or、-ed，词根 iacere 还构成 reject、inject、eject、subject。

latinIntro.en: Latin proicere 'throw forward' and its participle proiectum stand beside iacere 'throw'. The -ject family is a set of directions: re- back, in- in, e- out, pro- forward.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 proicere“向前抛”及其分词 proiectum 旁边是 iacere“投”。-ject 词族是一组方向：re- 向后、in- 向内、e- 向外、pro- 向前。
