definition_zh: 延长；拉长；使持续更久
definition_en: to make something last longer in time, or to stretch it out in length
core_image: 两只手抓住一根绳子，往两头慢慢拉，绳子变得更长
scene: 会谈已经拖到深夜，桌上的人都看着钟，谁也不愿先起身。The chairman refused to prolong the discussion and closed the meeting.
sceneCN: 这里取「延长、使持续更久」的意思（第 1 个义项：让某件事持续更久）；句意为主席不愿再把讨论拖长，于是宣布散会。

pos.zh: 延长；拉长；使（时间）持续更久

derivatives.zh: 由 prolong 加 -ation 构成，义为「延长；延期」
由 prolong 的过去分词转成的形容词，义为「持续很久的；长时间的」

senses.title: To make something last longer
senses.definition: to make an event, a state or a period continue for a longer time
senses.definitionCN: 使某个事件、状态或时期持续更久
senses.example: Nothing could prolong the summer beyond September.
senses.exampleCN: 没有什么能让夏天延续到九月之后。
senses.why: Latin longus means long, and the prefix pro- pushes outward, so the word starts from stretching something out.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 longus 意为「长」，前缀 pro- 表示向外推，所以这个词的起点是「把东西往外拉长」。

senses.title: To make a hard experience drag on
senses.definition: to keep an unpleasant situation or feeling going when it could end
senses.definitionCN: 在本可结束时让不愉快的处境或感受继续下去
senses.example: Refusing to decide only prolonged the uncertainty for everyone.
senses.exampleCN: 迟迟不做决定，只是让所有人的不确定感拖得更久。
senses.why: If length can be added to anything, it can be added to pain, so the word often carries the sense of needlessly extending what people want to end.
senses.whyCN: 既然长度可以加在任何东西上，也能加在痛苦上，于是这个词常带「把人们盼着结束的事无谓地拖长」的意味。

senses.title: To stretch something out in length
senses.definition: to extend something in physical length, a formal or literary use
senses.definitionCN: 从物理长度上把某物拉长，属正式或文学用法
senses.example: The low sun prolonged every shadow across the field.
senses.exampleCN: 低垂的太阳把田野上每道影子都拉得很长。
senses.why: The oldest sense is simply long, and when the object is a shadow or a line the word returns to that plain idea of length.
senses.whyCN: 最古老的意思就是「长」，当宾语是影子或线条时，这个词又回到最朴素的长度概念。

intro.en: Prolong joins a Latin prefix of outward movement to the Latin word for long, and French carried the verb into English.
intro.cn: prolong 把表示向外运动的拉丁语前缀接在表示「长」的拉丁词上，再由法语把动词带进英语。

items.en: The prefix pro- meant forward or outward, and longus meant long, so the pair pictured something drawn out at length.
items.cn: 前缀 pro- 表示向前、向外，形容词 longus 表示长，两者合起来就是「往外拉长」。

items.en: Prolongare meant to lengthen, to draw out, and it was used of both time and physical extent.
items.cn: prolongare 意为加长、拉长，时间和空间长度都能用它。

items.en: Old French prolonger kept the verb's sense of making something last or reach further.
items.cn: 古法语 prolonger 保留了「使某物更持久、伸得更远」的意思。

items.en: Middle English took the verb and used it mostly in the sense of adding time to something.
items.cn: 中古英语借入这个动词，多指给某事加上时间。

items.en: Modern English uses prolong mainly for time, and keeps the physical sense in literary descriptions of light, shadows and lines.
items.cn: 现代英语的 prolong 主要用于时间，物理意义上的拉长则多见于对光、影与线条的文学描写。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers words built on the Latin adjective for long; the near-meaning group gathers verbs for adding extent or time.
note.cn: 形近组收同一拉丁「长」形容词上的词；近义组收表示加长长度或时间的动词。

entries.definition: To make something longer, especially in shape.
entries.definitionCN: 使某物变长，尤指形状上的拉长。

entries.definition: Long life, or the length of a life.
entries.definitionCN: 长寿；寿命的长短。

entries.definition: The distance east or west measured in degrees.
entries.definitionCN: 以度数计量的东西方向距离；经度。

entries.definition: To make something longer or larger in space or time.
entries.definitionCN: 在空间或时间上使某物更长或更大。

entries.definition: To become or make longer.
entries.definitionCN: 变长；使变长。

entries.definition: To pull something so that it covers more space.
entries.definitionCN: 把某物拉展到占更多空间。

entries.definition: To make something take longer than necessary.
entries.definitionCN: 使某事拖得比必要的时间更长。

normalIntro.en: The word is a rope being pulled longer, and its family keeps returning to length and to time added on.
normalIntro.cn: 这个词就是一根被拉长的绳子，同族词反复回到「长度」和「被加上去的时间」。

normal.en: Latin longus also gives English longitude, so the idea of length sits inside prolong from the start.
normal.cn: 拉丁语 longus 还给英语带来 longitude，所以「长度」这个观念从一开始就在 prolong 里面。

normal.en: The prefix pro- pushes outward, so the rope leaves the hand rather than staying still.
normal.cn: 前缀 pro- 表示向外推，所以绳子是离开手心、被拉出去的。

normal.en: Prolongation adds -ation to the verb: the act of making something longer.
normal.cn: prolongation 在动词后加 -ation，指「使某物变长」这件事。

normal.en: We prolong life, meetings and agony, but the word often leans towards what people already wish would end.
normal.cn: 我们说延长寿命、延长会议、延长痛苦，而这个词常偏向人们本来就盼着结束的事。

normal.en: The adjective prolonged comes straight from the past participle and describes anything that has been drawn out.
normal.cn: 形容词 prolonged 直接来自过去分词，描述任何被拉长了的事物。

abstract.en: Anything measured in time can be stretched, which is why a word for length ends up meaning delay.
abstract.cn: 凡是用时间衡量的东西都能被拉长，所以一个表示长度的词最后也指拖延。

abstract.en: Prolonging is rarely neutral: adding time to something people want to end is adding weight to it.
abstract.cn: 延长很少是中性的：给人们盼着结束的事加上时间，等于给它加上重量。

abstract.en: A shadow and a meeting can share one verb because both are lines that someone draws out.
abstract.cn: 影子和会议能共用一个动词，因为两者都是被谁拉长的一根线。

examples.en: Regular exercise can prolong your life.
examples.cn: 经常锻炼可以延长寿命。

examples.en: They prolonged the meeting by arguing over details.
examples.cn: 他们为细节争论，把会议拖长了。

examples.en: A prolonged drought has dried up the river.
examples.cn: 长久干旱使这条河干涸了。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「扑若龙」——往前一扑像条长龙，越拉越长，就是延长。

root: 拉丁语 pro-（向前、向外）+ longus（长）构成 prolongare，本义「往外拉长」，经古法语 prolonger 进入英语。

sensesIntro.en: The core is stretching something outward; the senses divide into added time, needlessly added suffering, and the older physical stretching.
sensesIntro.cn: 核心是「把东西往外拉长」；义项分成加上的时间、无谓拖长的痛苦，以及更古老的物理拉长。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: two hands pulling a rope apart so that it grows longer and longer.
core.cn: 核心意象：两只手抓住一根绳子往两头拉，绳子越拉越长。

branches.en: a meeting that nobody wants to end
branches.cn: 谁都不愿意散的会议

branches.en: a waiting room where the clock barely moves
branches.cn: 钟几乎不走的候诊室

branches.en: shadows stretching across a field at sunset
branches.cn: 日落时横过田野的长影

branches.en: a low sun drawing a long line of shadow
branches.cn: 低垂的太阳拖出一道长长的影子

branches.en: a decision put off until the worry grows
branches.cn: 被一再推迟、让焦虑加长的决定

intro.en: A Latin prefix of outward movement and the Latin adjective for long hold the word together; French supplied the verb form that English borrowed.
intro.cn: 表示向外运动的拉丁语前缀和表示「长」的拉丁语形容词共同支撑这个词，英语借入的动词形式来自法语。

latinIntro.en: Latin longus, long, and the verb prolongare, to lengthen, are the direct sources of the English word.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语形容词 longus（长）与动词 prolongare（加长）是英语这个词的直接来源。

definition_zh: 显要地位；声望；突出物；隆起；（天文）日珥；（地质）高地；显著
definition_en: the state of being important or well known, a part that bulges out, or a glowing arch of gas above the sun's surface
core_image: 平地上有一块石头明显高出周围，所有视线都被它吸过去
scene: 这里指「显要地位」。 The young researcher rose to prominence after her study on coral bleaching was widely cited.
sceneCN: 这里 prominence 是「崭露头角后的显要地位」（第 1 个义项：从众人中突出、被广泛注意）；句意：她关于珊瑚白化的研究被广泛引用后，这位年轻研究者声名鹊起。图中可辨识物件：人群之上高出半头的身影、被引用的论文页。

pos.zh: 显要地位；声望；突出物；日珥；显著

derivatives.zh: 即将发生的（同源前缀不同）

senses.title: Standing out among others
senses.definition: the state of being important, noticeable or well known in a field
senses.definitionCN: 在某一领域中重要、惹人注意或广为人知的状态
senses.example: The discovery brought the small laboratory to international prominence.
senses.exampleCN: 这一发现让这家小实验室在国际上声名显要。
senses.why: Prominere meant 'to stand out from a surface'. Move the image from rock to reputation and you get the social sense: a person who stands out from the crowd.
senses.whyCN: prominere 意为“从表面突出”。把意象从岩石移到名声，就得到社会义：一个从人群中凸显出来的人。

senses.title: A raised part of a surface
senses.definition: a part of a surface that rises above the surrounding level
senses.definitionCN: 高出周围水平面的表面部位
senses.example: A small prominence on the handle helps the thumb grip it.
senses.exampleCN: 手柄上一处小小的凸起帮助拇指抓握。
senses.why: The noun began with the body and the landscape: any bump that pushed itself forward from a flat surface was a prominence.
senses.whyCN: 这个名词最初用于身体与地貌：任何从平面向前顶出的凸块都叫 prominence。

senses.title: Being impossible to miss
senses.definition: the quality of attracting attention because of position, size or contrast
senses.definitionCN: 因位置、尺寸或对比而吸引注意的性质
senses.example: The warning label was placed with such prominence that no buyer could miss it.
senses.exampleCN: 警示标签被放在如此显眼的位置，没有买家会看不到。
senses.why: A thing that sticks out is naturally seen first. The abstract noun keeps that visual fact and applies it to labels, errors and headlines.
senses.whyCN: 突出的东西自然最先被看到。这个抽象名词保留了这个视觉事实，并把它用到标签、错误与标题上。

senses.title: A flame arch above the sun
senses.definition: a large, glowing cloud of gas extending from the sun's surface into its atmosphere
senses.definitionCN: 从太阳表面伸入大气层的巨大发光气体云
senses.example: During the eclipse, a huge prominence was visible at the moon's edge.
senses.exampleCN: 日食期间，月球边缘可见一道巨大的日珥。
senses.why: Astronomers needed a word for a part of the sun that projects beyond its disc, and borrowed the Latin term for a projecting part.
senses.whyCN: 天文学家需要一个词来指太阳圆盘之外伸出的部分，就借用了拉丁语里表示“突出部分”的词。

senses.title: A bony bump named by anatomists
senses.titleCN: 解剖学命名的骨性隆起
senses.definition: a raised area of bone, especially one that can be felt through the skin
senses.definitionCN: 骨头上凸起的区域，尤指能隔着皮肤摸到的部位
senses.example: The doctor pressed the prominence at the base of the wrist.
senses.exampleCN: 医生按压腕部基底的骨性隆凸。
senses.why: Anatomy adopted the same descriptive noun for landmarks on bone, where a prominence is exactly what the fingers feel.
senses.whyCN: 解剖学沿用同一个描述性名词来指骨性标志，因为在骨头上，突出物正是手指摸到的东西。

senses.title: High ground in a landscape
senses.definition: a hill, ridge or other raised feature standing above the surrounding land
senses.definitionCN: 高出周围地面的山丘、山脊或其他隆起地形
senses.example: The village sits on a rocky prominence above the flood plain.
senses.exampleCN: 村庄坐落在洪泛平原之上的一处岩石高地。
senses.why: Geographers use the word for terrain that rises above its surroundings, keeping the literal outward bulge at the scale of a landscape.
senses.whyCN: 地理学家用这个词指高出周围的地形，把字面上的外凸保留到景观尺度。

senses.title: Drawing the eye to a feature
senses.titleCN: 把视线引向某个显著特征
senses.definition: the degree to which a feature is emphasized or made to stand out visually
senses.definitionCN: 某一特征被强调或在视觉上被突出的程度
senses.example: The designer increased the prominence of the search box on every page.
senses.exampleCN: 设计师提高了搜索框在每个页面上的显著度。
senses.why: In design and typography, prominence measures how strongly an element pushes itself forward against its background.
senses.whyCN: 在设计与排版中，prominence 衡量一个元素相对于背景把自己向前推的强度。

senses.title: A notable feature of a thing
senses.titleCN: 事物中引人注目的特点
senses.definition: a salient or conspicuous feature that defines how something is noticed
senses.definitionCN: 使某物被人注意的显著或突出特点
senses.example: The most striking prominence of the old hall is its carved stone doorway.
senses.exampleCN: 这座旧厅最引人注目的特点，是它雕花的石门洞。
senses.why: The word can name the feature itself, not only the state: whatever makes an object noticeable is its prominence.
senses.whyCN: 这个词也能指特征本身，而不只是状态：凡是使物体引人注意的东西，就是它的显著之处。

intro.en: Prominence comes from Latin prominentia, the noun of prominere, 'to stand out or jut forward'. Pro- supplied the forward direction and minere supplied the jutting. Everything the word names today - a bump, a hill, a solar flame, a famous name - is something that pushes out from its surroundings.
intro.cn: prominence 来自拉丁名词 prominentia，出自动词 prominere“突出、向前伸出”。pro- 提供向前方向，minere 提供“伸出”。今天这个词命名的一切——凸块、山丘、日珥、名人——都是从周围环境中顶出来的东西。

items.en: Minere meant 'to jut, to overhang'. Its deeper origin is uncertain; it is generally linked with eminere and imminere, and a connection with mons 'mountain' has been suggested but not proved.
items.cn: minere 意为“伸出、悬突”，其更深来源不确定；一般认为它与 eminere、imminere 同族，也有人提出与 mons“山”相关，但未获证实。

items.en: Pro- 'forward' plus minere 'jut' gave prominere, 'to stand out, to project'. The verb pictured anything pushing itself out from a surface.
items.cn: pro-“向前”加 minere“伸出”构成 prominere“突出、外伸”。这个动词描画任何从表面向外顶出的东西。

items.en: The abstract noun named the state of jutting out. Late Latin used it for physical bulges before English borrowed it.
items.cn: 这个抽象名词表示“突出”的状态。在英语借入之前，晚期拉丁语已用它指身体上的隆起。

items.en: English first applied prominence to raised parts of the body and to hills, keeping the literal bulge.
items.cn: 英语最初把 prominence 用于身体的隆起部位与山丘，保留了字面上的“凸起”。

items.en: The same outward-standing image moved from space to society: a person of prominence stands out from the crowd.
items.cn: 同一个“向外突出”的意象从空间移向社会：有 prominence 的人从人群中凸显。

items.en: Solar prominences were named during eclipse observations, and anatomists standardized the term for bony landmarks.
items.cn: 日珥在日食观测中得名，解剖学家则把这个词固定用于骨性标志。

note.en: The look-alike group separates the noun from its adjective and adverb and from the eminence family. The meaning group compares kinds of standing out, from fame to physical bumps.
note.cn: 形近组区分名词与它的形容词、副词形式，以及 eminence 词族；词义组比较不同类型的“突出”，从名声到物理凸起。

entries.definition: standing out physically or socially. It describes the thing, while prominence names the quality or the bump.
entries.definitionCN: 在物理上或社会上突出的。它描述事物，而 prominence 命名性质或凸起本身。

entries.definition: in a noticeable position or manner. It modifies an action, as in 'prominently displayed'.
entries.definitionCN: 以显眼的位置或方式。它修饰动作，如“显眼地展示”。

entries.definition: high rank, distinction, or literally a height. It comes from eminere 'stand out', a sibling of prominere with a different prefix.
entries.definitionCN: 高位、卓越，或字面上的高地。它来自 eminere“突出”，是 prominere 的同胞词，只是前缀不同。

entries.definition: the state of being about to happen. It comes from imminere 'overhang', the same jutting verb with in- 'upon'.
entries.definitionCN: 即将发生的状态。它来自 imminere“悬临”，是同一个“伸出”动词加上 in-“在上”。

entries.definition: recognized superiority in a field. It is close to sense 01 but sounds more formal and more about rank.
entries.definitionCN: 在某领域被公认的优越地位。它接近第 1 义项，但更正式、更强调等级。

entries.definition: excellence or a quality that sets someone apart. It stresses difference in quality rather than visibility.
entries.definitionCN: 卓越或使人出众的品质。它强调品质上的差异，而非可见度。

entries.definition: something that bulges out. It is the plain word for sense 02, without the reputation sense.
entries.definitionCN: 凸出的东西。它是第 2 义项的平实说法，没有名声义。

entries.definition: the quality of standing out to attention. It is the technical term for senses 03 and 07.
entries.definitionCN: 在注意中凸显的性质。它是第 3 与第 7 义项的技术说法。

normalIntro.en: These hooks keep one picture: a bump that rises above a flat surface. Fame, hills, sun flames, bones and labels are all versions of that bump.
normalIntro.cn: 这些记忆钩只保留一个画面：从平面上升起的一块凸起。名声、山丘、日焰、骨头与标签都是这块凸起的变体。

normal.en: Split it as pro + min + ence: forward + jut + noun. A prominence is something that juts forward.
normal.cn: 拆成 pro + min + ence：向前、伸出、名词。prominence 就是向前伸出的东西。

normal.en: Picture a stone slab with one pebble glued on top: the pebble is a prominence.
normal.cn: 想象一块石板上粘着一颗小石子：那颗石子就是 prominence。

normal.en: Move the pebble to a village on a hill and you have the landscape sense.
normal.cn: 把小石子换成一坐落在山丘上的村庄，就得到地貌义。

normal.en: Move it to a crowd and the person whose head rises above the rest has prominence.
normal.cn: 把它移到人群：高出众人一头的人就有了 prominence。

normal.en: Move it to the sun's edge and the rising gas arch is a solar prominence.
normal.cn: 把它移到太阳边缘，升起的气体拱就是日珥。

abstract.en: The word always compares: without a surrounding level, nothing can be prominent.
abstract.cn: 这个词始终在比较：没有周围的水平面，就没有东西能算突出。

abstract.en: Keep the two halves apart: prominence is the bump or the fame, prominent is the adjective you use to describe it.
abstract.cn: 分清两半：prominence 是凸起或名声本身，prominent 是你用来描述它的形容词。

abstract.en: The solar sense shows how literal the word stays: astronomers still mean a part that projects beyond the disc.
abstract.cn: 日珥义说明这个词有多字面：天文学家指的仍是伸出圆盘之外的部分。

examples.en: Her early work on soil bacteria brought her sudden prominence in the field.
examples.cn: 她早期关于土壤细菌的研究让她在该领域骤然成名。

examples.en: A bony prominence behind the ear marks where the muscle attaches.
examples.cn: 耳后的一处骨性隆凸标出了肌肉附着的位置。

examples.en: The editor gave the climate report unusual prominence on page one.
examples.cn: 编辑把气候报道放在了头版异常显眼的位置。

dict_mnemonic.text: 谐音“扑罗米能斯”：一粒米能顶在平面上，就是一处凸起。

root: 拉丁 prominere“突出、外伸”（pro- 向前 + minere 伸出），名词 prominentia；核心是“从周围平面顶出来的一块”。

sensesIntro.en: Every sense describes something that rises above its surroundings: a reputation above the crowd, a bump above a surface, a label above other text, gas above the sun's disc, bone above the skin, a hill above the plain, an element above its background, a feature above the rest of an object.
sensesIntro.cn: 每个义项都描述高出周围环境的东西：高于人群的名声、高出表面的凸起、压过其他文字的标签、伸出日面之外的气体、顶着皮肤的骨头、高出平原的山丘、压过背景的元素、盖过物件其余部分的特点。

core.en: One surface, one part raised above it, and attention drawn to the raised part.
core.cn: 一个平面，一块高出它的部分，注意力被引向这块凸起。

branches.en: PHYSICAL: a part rises above the surface that carries it.
branches.cn: 物理：一部分高出承载它的表面。

branches.en: ATTENTION: the raised part is what the eye finds first.
branches.cn: 注意：凸起部分是眼睛最先找到的东西。

branches.en: SKY: gas rises above the sun's visible disc.
branches.cn: 天空：气体高出于太阳可见的圆盘。

branches.en: TERRAIN: bone and land repeat the same raised shape.
branches.cn: 地形：骨头与土地重复同一种隆起形状。

branches.en: REPUTATION: a person rises above the crowd and is widely known.
branches.cn: 名声：一个人高出人群之上，被广泛知晓。

intro.en: Prominence is pro- plus minere plus the noun suffix -entia. The items below follow the same jutting verb through its adjective, adverb and the sibling prefixes e- and in-.
intro.cn: prominence 由 pro-、minere 与名词后缀 -entia 构成。下列条目沿着同一个“伸出”动词，走过形容词、副词以及同胞前缀 e- 与 in-。

latinIntro.en: The Latin entries give the jutting verb, its abstract noun and the bare root. They show why eminence, imminent and prominence look like cousins.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语条目给出“伸出”动词、抽象名词与裸露词根，说明为什么 eminence、imminent 与 prominence 看起来像表亲。

items.example: The bridge gained prominence after the flood.
items.exampleCN: 洪水过后这座桥变得重要起来。

items.example: A prominent oak stood at the gate.
items.exampleCN: 门口立着一棵显眼的橡树。

items.example: Her name appeared prominently on the cover.
items.exampleCN: 她的名字显眼地出现在封面上。

items.example: The surgeon reached eminence in her thirties.
items.exampleCN: 这位外科医生三十多岁时便已卓越成名。

items.example: An eminent historian opened the session.
items.exampleCN: 一位著名历史学家主持了会议。

items.meaning: about to happen, as if hanging over
items.example: Storm clouds warned of imminent rain.
items.exampleCN: 乌云预示着雨即将到来。

items.meaning: the state of being about to happen
items.example: The imminence of the deadline forced a decision.
items.exampleCN: 截止期限迫近，迫使人们作出决定。

items.meaningCN: 出类拔萃的；首屈一指的
items.example: She is the preeminent scholar of the period.
items.exampleCN: 她是该时期首屈一指的学者。

definition_zh: 突出的；显眼的；著名的；显要的；重要的；（特征）显著的；（结构）外凸的
definition_en: standing out from a surface or from other people, and therefore easy to notice or important
core_image: 一块石头从墙面上凸出来，走过的人都先看见它
scene: 她的名字出现在海报最显眼的位置。A prominent sandstone arch frames the entrance to the old library.
sceneCN: 这里 prominent 是「向外突出的」（第 3 个义项：结构从墙面伸出、形成门框）；句意：一道突出的砂岩拱券框住了老图书馆的入口。图中可辨识物件：从墙面伸出的拱券、被框住的入口；对应第 1 个义项。

pos.zh: 突出的；显眼的；著名的；显要的；显著的

senses.title: Well known and respected
senses.definition: widely known and respected in a particular field
senses.definitionCN: 在某一领域广为人知并受敬重
senses.example: A prominent economist warned that the housing boom would end.
senses.exampleCN: 一位著名经济学家警告说房地产繁荣将会结束。
senses.why: Prominens meant 'standing out'. Fame is social standing out: the person rises visibly above the ordinary level of the profession.
senses.whyCN: prominens 意为“突出的”。名声就是社会意义上的突出：这个人明显高出于行业的一般水平。

senses.title: Holding an important position
senses.definition: having an important or influential position in an organization or society
senses.definitionCN: 在组织或社会中居于重要或有影响力的位置
senses.example: Several prominent families opposed the new tax.
senses.exampleCN: 几个显赫家族反对这项新税。
senses.why: The word moves from visibility to power: a prominent family is one whose name stands out in public affairs and can therefore sway them.
senses.whyCN: 这个词从可见度转到权力：显赫家族的名字在公共事务中突出，因此能左右事务。

senses.title: Sticking out from a surface
senses.definition: rising or projecting above the surrounding surface
senses.definitionCN: 高出或伸出周围表面的
senses.example: The old house had prominent stone arches over every window.
senses.exampleCN: 这座老房子每扇窗上都有突出的石拱。
senses.why: This is the literal core: the thing itself pushes forward beyond the plane it belongs to, so it catches the eye before anything else.
senses.whyCN: 这是字面核心：事物本身顶出所属平面之外，所以比其他东西更早抓住视线。

senses.title: Impossible to overlook
senses.titleCN: 一眼就能看到、难以忽略
senses.definition: placed or shaped so that it is noticed immediately
senses.definitionCN: 放置或造型使其立刻被注意到
senses.example: The safety instructions were printed in a prominent band of red.
senses.exampleCN: 安全说明被印在一条醒目的红色带子上。
senses.why: When designers call a label prominent, they mean it wins the competition for attention against everything around it.
senses.whyCN: 当设计师说某个标签 prominent，意思是它在与周围一切争夺注意力时胜出。

senses.title: Clearly visible in a feature
senses.definition: clearly marked or easily observed, as of a sign or symptom
senses.definitionCN: 指迹象或症状明显、易于观察
senses.example: The first prominent symptom was a persistent dry cough.
senses.exampleCN: 最先出现的明显症状是持续干咳。
senses.why: In medicine the word marks what a clinician cannot miss: a sign that presents itself plainly rather than hiding in the background.
senses.whyCN: 在医学中，这个词标记临床医生不会漏掉的东西：一个直接呈现、不藏在背景里的征象。

senses.title: The leading element
senses.definition: the most important or noticeable element among several
senses.definitionCN: 若干要素中最重要或最引人注意的一个
senses.example: Loss of trust is the most prominent theme in the interviews.
senses.exampleCN: 失去信任是这些访谈中最突出的主题。
senses.why: Among competing elements, the prominent one is the one that stands above the rest of the set, much as a bump stands above a surface.
senses.whyCN: 在相互竞争的要素中，突出的那一个是高出其余部分的，就像凸起高出表面。

senses.title: Socially conspicuous
senses.definition: attracting public notice because of wealth, rank or family name
senses.definitionCN: 因财富、地位或家族名望而引人注目
senses.example: The wedding was attended by the town's most prominent citizens.
senses.exampleCN: 镇上最显要的市民都出席了这场婚礼。
senses.why: The social sense specializes in public notice: not merely famous for work, but visible because of rank or wealth.
senses.whyCN: 社会义专门指向公众注意：不仅因工作而出名，更因地位或财富而显眼。

senses.title: Standing out to the eye or ear
senses.definition: visually or acoustically strong enough to dominate the surrounding pattern
senses.definitionCN: 在视觉或听觉上足够强，压过周围的图案或声音
senses.example: A prominent blue stripe runs through the whole fabric.
senses.exampleCN: 一道醒目的蓝色条纹贯穿整块布料。
senses.why: Design and music use the word for the element that dominates the pattern, whether a colour or a beat.
senses.whyCN: 设计与音乐用这个词指压过整体图案的元素，无论是一种颜色还是一个节拍。

intro.en: Prominent is the present participle of Latin prominere, 'to stand out, to project'. Pro- gives the forward push and minere gives the jutting. English borrowed it in the 17th century and let it spread from rocks and bones to reputations, symptoms and design.
intro.cn: prominent 是拉丁 prominere“突出、外伸”的现在分词。pro- 提供向前的推力，minere 提供“伸出”。英语在 17 世纪借入，并让它从岩石与骨骼扩展到名声、症状与设计。

items.en: Minere meant 'to jut or overhang'. Its deeper origin is uncertain; connections with eminere and imminere are generally accepted, while a link to mons 'mountain' remains unproved.
items.cn: minere 意为“伸出、悬突”，更深来源不确定；与 eminere、imminere 的关联一般被接受，而与 mons“山”的联系尚未证实。

items.en: Prominere combined pro- 'forward' with minere 'jut' and meant 'to stand out, to project'. Its participle prominens described whatever was doing the standing out.
items.cn: prominere 由 pro-“向前”与 minere“伸出”组成，意为“突出、外伸”。其分词 prominens 描述正在突出的东西。

items.en: The participle was already used for projecting parts of buildings and bodies, so the adjective carried a physical meaning from the start.
items.cn: 这个分词已用于建筑与身体的外凸部位，因此形容词从一开始就带有物理含义。

items.en: English adopted prominent for physical projections first, then extended it to anything that stood above its surroundings in importance.
items.cn: 英语先借 prominent 指物理凸起，再扩展到任何在重要性上高出周围环境的事物。

items.en: Newspapers made 'prominent citizens' a familiar phrase, and the adjective became the standard word for public standing.
items.cn: 报纸使“显要市民”成为常见说法，这个形容词也成为表示公共地位的标准词。

items.en: Clinical writing adopted prominent for signs that stand out, while design and music used it for elements that dominate a pattern.
items.cn: 临床写作采用 prominent 指明显的征象，设计与音乐则用它指压过整体图案的元素。

note.en: The look-alike group separates the adjective from its noun, adverb and the eminence family. The meaning group contrasts being famous, being obvious and being physically raised.
note.cn: 形近组区分形容词与它的名词、副词形式及 eminence 词族；词义组比较“有名”“明显”与“物理凸起”。

entries.definition: the quality of standing out, or the raised part itself. It names what prominent describes.
entries.definitionCN: 突出的性质，或凸起本身。它命名 prominent 所描述的东西。

entries.definition: in a way that is easy to notice. It tells how something is placed or shown.
entries.definitionCN: 以容易注意的方式。它说明某物如何被放置或展示。

entries.definition: high rank or a height. It comes from eminere, the same jutting verb with e- 'out' instead of pro- 'forward'.
entries.definitionCN: 高位或高地。它来自 eminere，同一个“伸出”动词，只是用 e-“向外”取代 pro-“向前”。

entries.definition: lasting forever. It looks similar but comes from per- 'through' plus manere 'to remain', a completely different root.
entries.definitionCN: 永久的。它看起来相似，却来自 per-“贯穿”加 manere“停留”，词根完全不同。

entries.definition: distinguished and highly respected. It is close to sense 01 but sounds more formal and more about rank.
entries.definitionCN: 卓越且深受敬重的。它接近第 1 义项，但更正式、更强调等级。

entries.definition: clearly visible, often because of unusual appearance. It stresses being seen, while prominent stresses standing above a level.
entries.definitionCN: 明显可见的，常因外形不寻常。它强调被看见，而 prominent 强调高出某一水平。

entries.definition: easy to see or feel. It is the plain everyday word for sense 04.
entries.definitionCN: 容易看到或感觉到的。它是第 4 义项的日常说法。

entries.definition: sticking out physically. It is the narrow word for sense 03, with no fame or importance attached.
entries.definitionCN: 物理上伸出的。它是第 3 义项的窄义说法，不附带名声或重要性。

normalIntro.en: These hooks pin the word to one raised shape, then let it travel from walls to faces, from symptoms to fame.
normalIntro.cn: 这些记忆钩把词钉在一个隆起的形状上，再让它从墙面走到面孔、从症状走到名声。

normal.en: Split it as pro + min + ent: forward + jut + adjective. Anything that juts forward is prominent.
normal.cn: 拆成 pro + min + ent：向前、伸出、形容词。凡是向前伸出的就是 prominent。

normal.en: Picture a wall with one brick pushed out: your hand finds that brick first.
normal.cn: 想象一面墙里有一块砖被顶了出来：你的手最先摸到那块砖。

normal.en: Prominent teeth and a prominent nose are the same brick, moved to a face.
normal.cn: 突出的牙齿与高鼻梁就是同一块砖，被移到了脸上。

normal.en: A prominent symptom is the brick in a medical chart: the one the doctor circles.
normal.cn: 明显症状就是病历里的那块砖：医生会把它圈出来。

normal.en: A prominent scientist is the same brick in a crowd: the one the reporters call first.
normal.cn: 著名科学家就是人群里的那块砖：记者最先打电话给他。

abstract.en: The word always needs a background: a bump on a bump is not prominent, only a bump on a flat surface is.
abstract.cn: 这个词始终需要背景：凸起上的凸起并不突出，只有平面上的凸起才突出。

abstract.en: Keep fame and shape in one frame: the person stands out socially exactly as the brick stands out physically.
abstract.cn: 把名声与形状放在同一个框架里：人在社会上突出，正如砖头在物理上突出。

abstract.en: Watch the suffix: prominent describes, prominence names, prominently tells how.
abstract.cn: 留意后缀：prominent 描述，prominence 命名，prominently 说明方式。

examples.en: A prominent legal scholar argued that the ruling was too broad.
examples.cn: 一位著名法学学者主张该判决范围过宽。

examples.en: The bird's most prominent feature is the bright red crest on its head.
examples.cn: 这种鸟最显著的特征是头顶鲜红的冠羽。

examples.en: Warning signs were mounted in prominent positions along the cliff path.
examples.cn: 警示牌被安装在悬崖步道的显眼位置。

dict_mnemonic.text: 谐音“扑罗米能特”：一块米能特别突出，从平面上顶出来。

root: 拉丁 prominere 的现在分词 prominens“突出的”（pro- 向前 + minere 伸出）；核心是“从平面顶出来、一眼看见”。

sensesIntro.en: The eight senses all describe one thing standing above another: a scholar above peers, a family above society, a stone above a wall, a label above text, a symptom above silence, a theme above its rivals, a citizen above the town, a stripe above the fabric.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项都在描述一物高出另一物：学者高出同行，家族高出社会，石头高出墙面，标签压过文字，症状压过沉默，主题压过其他主题，市民高出小镇，条纹压过布料。

core.en: A part that rises above its background, so that attention lands on it before anything else.
core.cn: 一部分高出背景，因此注意力先落在它上面。

branches.en: PEOPLE: a person rises above peers by reputation or position.
branches.cn: 人：一个人凭名声或地位高出同侪。

branches.en: SHAPE: a part pushes out of its surface and dominates the pattern.
branches.cn: 形状：一部分顶出表面，压过整体图案。

branches.en: VISIBILITY: what stands out is noticed at once, in a room or on a chart.
branches.cn: 可见度：突出的东西立刻被注意到，无论在房间里还是在图表上。

branches.en: COMPETITION: among rival elements, one stands above the rest of the set.
branches.cn: 竞争：在相互竞争的要素中，有一个高出其余。

branches.en: SOCIETY: rank and wealth make a family visible in public life.
branches.cn: 社会：地位与财富让一个家族在公共生活中显眼。

intro.en: Prominent is a Latin participle used as an adjective. The items below show the same jutting verb through noun, adverb and the sibling prefixes e- and in-.
intro.cn: prominent 是拉丁分词用作形容词。下列条目沿着同一个“伸出”动词，走过名词、副词与同胞前缀 e-、in-。

latinIntro.en: The Latin entries give the verb and its participle. They explain why prominent, prominence and eminence keep the same core image.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语条目给出动词与分词，解释为什么 prominent、prominence 与 eminence 保持同一个核心意象。

items.example: A prominent ridge hides the valley from view.
items.exampleCN: 一道突出的山脊挡住了山谷的视线。

items.meaning: the state of standing out; a bump
items.example: The tower's prominence makes it a landmark.
items.exampleCN: 这座塔的突出使它成为地标。

items.example: The flag was prominently hung above the door.
items.exampleCN: 旗帜显眼地挂在门上方。

items.example: The hill's eminence gives a view of the bay.
items.exampleCN: 这座山丘的高起让人能看到海湾。

items.example: An eminent critic praised the first novel.
items.exampleCN: 一位著名评论家称赞了这部处女作。
锈蚀表明随时可能坍塌。

items.example: His reputation was supereminent in his lifetime.

items.exampleCN: 这个计划非常切实可行。

definition_zh: 许诺；答应；承诺；诺言；希望；前途
definition_en: to say firmly that one will do something, the statement so made, and the signs that something good is likely to come
core_image: 两只手伸出去一击为定，把一句还看不见的话变成双方都得守住的东西
scene: 临行前，父亲把旧钥匙放进儿子手里，说定秋天一定回来看那棵老树。Before he left, he promised to come back for the harvest.
sceneCN: 这里表示「许诺、答应」（第 1 个义项：明确说出自己一定会做某事）；句意为他在离开之前答应回来参加秋收。

derivatives.zh: 由 promise 加 -ing 构成，义为「有前途的；有希望的」
由拉丁词干 promiss- 加 -ory 构成，义为「承诺的；约定的」，常见于法律文书
由 promising 再加 -ly 构成，义为「有希望地；看来不错地」

senses.title: To say firmly that one will do something
senses.definition: to tell someone that you will certainly do something, so that the other person can count on it
senses.definitionCN: 明确告诉某人自己一定会做某事，使对方可以指望
senses.example: She promised to call as soon as she landed.
senses.exampleCN: 她答应一下飞机就打电话。
senses.why: The Latin verb sent a word forward toward the listener, so the act begins as a message travelling out of the speaker's mouth.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁动词的意思是「把话往前送」，所以这个动作起初是一句话从说话人嘴里飞向听者。

senses.title: A statement that one will certainly do something
senses.definition: a statement in which someone says that they will certainly do something
senses.definitionCN: 某人说定自己一定会做某事的说法
senses.example: He kept every promise he made that summer.
senses.exampleCN: 那个夏天他许下的每个诺言都守住了。
senses.why: Once spoken, the message no longer belongs to the speaker alone; it can be kept, quoted or thrown back, which is how the verb turns into the thing itself.
senses.whyCN: 话一出口就不再只属于说话人，它会被收着、被引用、被拿出来对质；动词就这样变成了那个被送出的东西。

senses.title: To show signs that something good is likely
senses.definition: to give signs that something good or important is likely to happen
senses.definitionCN: 显出好结果或重要事情很可能发生的迹象
senses.example: The early sales figures promise a strong year.
senses.exampleCN: 早期销售数字预示着这一年会很不错。
senses.why: A pledge always leans toward a future that has not arrived; when clouds or numbers do the leaning, the word keeps only that forward look and drops the speaker.
senses.whyCN: 诺言本就朝着一个还没到来的将来倾斜；当乌云或数字在倾斜时，这个词只留下「朝前指」的动作，说话人则退场了。

senses.title: The quality of seeming likely to succeed
senses.definition: the quality of seeming likely to succeed, especially in a young person or a new project
senses.definitionCN: 看起来很可能成功的那份质地，尤指年轻人或新项目身上的
senses.example: The young pianist showed promise from her first recital.
senses.exampleCN: 这位年轻钢琴家从第一场独奏会起就显出前途。
senses.why: If the good thing is promised but has not arrived, the noun can name that waiting good thing directly, and English does so especially for talent that has not yet proved itself.
senses.whyCN: 如果好事已被许诺却还没到，名词就能直接指那件正在等着的好事；英语尤其用它来说尚未证明自己的才华。

intro.en: Promise comes from a Latin verb meaning to send a word forward, and the English word still has the shape of a message flying toward someone who will hold you to it.
intro.cn: promise 来自一个意为「把话往前送」的拉丁动词，这个词至今保持着「一句话飞向对方，对方据此要求你兑现」的形状。

items.en: Mittere meant to send or to let go, and it sits inside many English words about sending and releasing.
items.cn: mittere 意为送出、放走，是许多表示「送出、释放」的英语词里的那个成分。

items.en: The prefix pro- pushed the sending forward, so promittere meant to send a word forth, that is, to give someone your word.
items.cn: 前缀 pro- 把「送」推向前面，于是 promittere 意为把话送出去，也就是向人许下诺言。

items.en: The participle promissum named the thing sent forth rather than the sending, and it is the direct source of the noun.
items.cn: 分词 promissum 指被送出的那个东西，而不是送的动作，是名词义项的直接来源。

items.en: Old French kept the noun as promesse, meaning a pledge, and English borrowed it with the ending reshaped as promise.
items.cn: 古法语把这个名词写作 promesse，意为诺言，英语借入时把词尾改成 promise。

items.en: English uses the verb for giving one's word and the noun for the word given, then stretches both to the hopeful signs that point at a good future.
items.cn: 现代英语用动词指给出承诺，用名词指给出的那句话，再把两者扩展到指向美好未来的种种迹象。

note.en: The first group shares the Latin verb of sending, including a legal pair for the two sides of a pledge; the second group gathers words for solemn promises.
note.cn: 第一组共用表示「送出」的拉丁动词，还包括指承诺双方的一对法律用语；第二组收表示郑重许诺的词。

entries.definition: Relating to a promise, especially one that has legal force.
entries.definitionCN: 与承诺有关的，尤指具有法律效力的承诺。

entries.definition: In law, the person to whom a promise is made.
entries.definitionCN: 法律用语，指接受承诺的一方。

entries.definition: In law, the person who makes a promise.
entries.definitionCN: 法律用语，指做出承诺的一方。

entries.definition: A statement assumed true as a basis for reasoning; it shares the Latin verb of sending but not the sense of pledging.
entries.definitionCN: 推理时被当作前提的陈述；与本词共用拉丁「送」动词，但没有许诺之义。

entries.definition: A serious promise, often backed by something given as security.
entries.definitionCN: 郑重的承诺，常以某物作担保。

entries.definition: A solemn promise, especially one about marriage or faith.
entries.definitionCN: 庄严的誓愿，尤指关于婚姻或信仰的。

entries.definition: A formal promise made before a witness or on something sacred.
entries.definitionCN: 在见证人面前或对神圣之物做出的正式承诺。

entries.definition: A statement meant to give someone confidence about the future.
entries.definitionCN: 意在让人对将来安心的说法。

normalIntro.en: Every sense keeps the picture of a word sent forward: someone speaks, the word travels, and the listener is then entitled to expect something.
normalIntro.cn: 每个义项都保留着「一句话被送出去」的画面：有人开口，话飞过去，听的人从此有权期待某件事。

normal.en: Mittere is Latin for to send, and pro- pushes it forward, so promittere is to send a word ahead of you.
normal.cn: mittere 是拉丁语的「送」，pro- 把它往前推，所以 promittere 就是「把话先送出去」。

normal.en: Promissum is the thing that was sent, which is why the noun means the word given and not the act of giving it.
normal.cn: promissum 是被送出的那个东西，所以名词义指说出的那句话，而不是说这句话的动作。

normal.en: Promising adds -ing to describe someone or something that already looks like a coming success.
normal.cn: promising 加 -ing，用来形容已经显出成功样子的年轻人或事物。

normal.en: Weather that promises rain keeps only the forward-pointing part of a pledge, with nobody actually pledging.
normal.cn: 天气 promise rain 只保留了许诺中「朝前指」的那一半，并没有谁真的在许诺。

normal.en: Keep and break fit promise because a pledge is treated like an object held in the hand or dropped on the floor.
normal.cn: keep 与 break 能配 promise，是因为诺言被当成手里的东西：可以握住，也可以摔掉。

abstract.en: A promise is a word lent forward in time, and the debt is settled when that future finally arrives.
abstract.cn: 诺言是一句被借到将来的话，等那个将来真的到来，债才算还清。

abstract.en: One word covers a pledge and a hopeful sign because both are the present pointing at something not yet here.
abstract.cn: 同一个词既指誓言，也指好兆头，因为两者都是「现在」在指向尚未到来的东西。

abstract.en: To promise is to make your future self answerable to another person's memory of what you said.
abstract.cn: 许诺就是让你的将来那个自己去面对别人记住的那句话。

examples.en: She promised to send the file before noon.
examples.cn: 她答应中午前把文件发过去。

examples.en: He broke his promise and never mentioned it again.
examples.cn: 他违背了诺言，此后再没提起。

examples.en: The new treatment promises to help patients who failed older drugs.
examples.cn: 这种新疗法有望帮助那些对旧药无效的病人。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「普若米事」——说出口的事像米粒撒出去，收不回来，只能认账；记住 promise 是许诺。

root: 拉丁语 pro-（向前）+ mittere（送、放出）→ promittere（把话送出去、许下诺言）→ promissum（被送出的承诺），经古法语 promesse 进入英语；同族词多与「送出、放出」有关，premise 与本词共用 mittere，但前缀不同、意义也走远。

sensesIntro.en: The core sense is a word sent forward to bind the speaker; from it come the pledge itself, the hopeful sign, and the promise that a future holds.
sensesIntro.cn: 核心义是「一句被送出去、用来约束说话人的话」；由此分出那句诺言本身、指向好结果的迹象，以及关于前途的希望。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: two hands meeting in a hard clasp, turning spoken words into something both sides must keep.
core.cn: 核心意象：两只手用力一击，把说出口的话变成双方都得守住的东西。

branches.en: a hand stretched out before the sentence is finished
branches.cn: 话还没说完，手已经伸了出去

branches.en: a written pledge folded away in a drawer
branches.cn: 写下来的承诺折好收进抽屉

branches.en: dark clouds carrying the smell of coming rain
branches.cn: 带着雨意的乌云压在天边

branches.en: a young musician whose future seems already waiting
branches.cn: 前途仿佛已经在前方等着的年轻乐手

branches.en: one word for a vow and for a hope
branches.cn: 同一个词既指誓言，也指希望

intro.en: A Latin verb of sending, its forward prefix, and the endings that turn the message into a noun and an adjective hold the word together.
intro.cn: 表示「送」的拉丁动词、表示向前的前缀，以及把这句话变成名词与形容词的词尾，共同支撑这个词。

latinIntro.en: The Latin verb promittere and its participle promissum are the reliable cognates behind the English noun.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语动词 promittere 及其分词 promissum，是英语这个词可靠的同源词。

items.meaning: to send forth a word, to promise
that which is sent forth, a promise

latinEntries.meaning: to send forth a word, to promise

definition_zh: 提升；晋升；促进；推动；推销；宣传；（棋）升变
definition_en: to move someone or something to a higher position, or to encourage its growth or acceptance
core_image: 一只手把一个人从台阶的下层托到上一层
scene: 公司年会上，经理把一位做了五年的一线员工叫到台前。The manager decided to promote her from team leader to department head after five years on the line.
sceneCN: 这里 promote 是「提升、晋升」（第 1 个义项：把某人移到更高的职位）；句意：经理决定把在一线做了五年的她从组长提升为部门主管。图中可辨识物件：舞台、晋升名单、新工牌、握手、掌声；对应第 1 个义项。

pos.zh: 提升；晋升；促进；推销；宣传

senses.title: Advance someone in rank
senses.definition: to move a person to a higher position or rank
senses.definitionCN: 把某人移到更高的职位或等级
senses.example: She was promoted to department head.
senses.exampleCN: 她被提升为部门主管。
senses.why: Latin promovere means 'move forward': pro- 'forward' plus movere 'to move'. A promotion moves a person up the institutional ladder.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 promovere 意为“向前移动”：pro-“向前”加 movere“移动”。晋升就是把一个人沿机构的梯子往上移。

senses.title: Encourage growth or success
senses.definition: to help something grow, develop, or succeed
senses.definitionCN: 帮助某事物成长、发展或成功
senses.example: The policy promotes small businesses.
senses.exampleCN: 这项政策促进小企业。
senses.why: The object changes from a person to a process: what is promoted is made to move forward. The word becomes a general verb of support.
senses.whyCN: 对象从人变成过程：被 promote 的东西被推着向前。这个词变成泛用的支持动词。

senses.title: Advertise or publicize
senses.definition: to make a product, idea, or event known in order to sell or gain support
senses.definitionCN: 使产品、理念或活动为人所知，以销售或争取支持
senses.example: The company promotes its new phone online.
senses.exampleCN: 公司在网上推销新手机。
senses.why: Commerce borrows the ladder image: a product is moved forward in the market, pushed toward buyers. Promotion becomes the noun of marketing.
senses.whyCN: 商业借来梯子意象：产品在市场中被向前推，推向买家。promotion 于是成了营销名词。

senses.title: Move a pupil to the next grade
senses.definition: to advance a student to the next class or level
senses.definitionCN: 把学生升到下一个班级或年级
senses.example: All students were promoted to the next grade.
senses.exampleCN: 所有学生都升到了下一个年级。
senses.why: Schools use the same upward motion: a pupil moves from one level to the next. The opposite, to hold back, keeps the spatial logic.
senses.whyCN: 学校用同一个向上运动：学生从一级移到下一级。反义词“留级”保留同样的空间逻辑。

senses.title: Cause an idea or cause to advance
senses.definition: to help a cause, idea, or value become stronger or more accepted
senses.definitionCN: 帮助事业、理念或价值变得更强、更被接受
senses.example: The campaign promotes healthy eating.
senses.exampleCN: 这场运动推广健康饮食。
senses.why: Public language treats values as objects that can be pushed forward. To promote peace is to give it momentum in the world.
senses.whyCN: 公共语言把价值当作可被推向前方的物体。promote peace 就是让和平在世界上获得动量。

senses.title: Advance a pawn in chess
senses.definition: in chess, to move a pawn to the last rank and replace it with a stronger piece
senses.definitionCN: 国际象棋中，把兵走到对方底线并换成更强的子
senses.example: The pawn was promoted to a queen.
senses.exampleCN: 那个兵升变为后。
senses.why: Chess gives the ladder literal form: a lowly pawn reaches the far rank and becomes a queen. The metaphor of advancement becomes a rule of the game.
senses.whyCN: 国际象棋把梯子变成字面规则：卑微的兵走到远端，变成后。“晋升”隐喻成了游戏规则。

senses.title: Move a team to a higher league
senses.definition: in sport, to move a club or player to a higher division
senses.definitionCN: 体育中把俱乐部或选手升到更高级别
senses.example: The club was promoted to the first division.
senses.exampleCN: 该俱乐部升入甲级。
senses.why: League tables rank teams by results. Promotion is the reward for finishing high, and relegation is its mirror. The word makes sport a visible ladder.
senses.whyCN: 联赛积分榜按成绩给球队排序。升级是名列前茅的奖赏，降级是它的镜像。这个词让体育成了一条可见的梯子。

senses.title: Accelerate a chemical reaction
senses.definition: in chemistry, to increase the rate of a reaction
senses.definitionCN: 化学中加快反应速率
senses.example: The catalyst promotes the reaction.
senses.exampleCN: 催化剂促进该反应。
senses.why: A catalyst moves a reaction forward without being consumed. Science uses promote for any agent that speeds a process, keeping the 'move forward' core.
senses.whyCN: 催化剂推动反应向前，自身不被消耗。科学用 promote 指任何加速过程的因素，保留“向前移动”核心。

senses.title: Push forward physically (archaic)
senses.definition: in older usage, to move something forward in space
senses.definitionCN: 旧用法：把某物在空间中向前推
senses.example: The crowd promoted him toward the door.
senses.exampleCN: 人群把他推向门口。
senses.why: This is the literal Latin sense, now rare. Modern English keeps it mainly in the abstract ladder, but the physical push is still visible in the metaphor.
senses.whyCN: 这是拉丁字面义，现已罕见。现代英语主要在抽象梯子中保留它，但物理的“推”仍能在隐喻中看见。

intro.en: Promote is a forward-motion word: Latin promovere joins pro- 'forward' to movere 'to move'. English borrowed it in the late 14c. and then applied the same push to careers, causes, products, and pawns.
intro.cn: promote 是一个向前运动的词：拉丁语 promovere 把 pro-“向前”与 movere“移动”结合。英语在 14 世纪末借入，随后把同一推动用到职业、事业、产品与棋子。

items.en: First recorded with the sense 'advance, further, encourage'.
items.cn: 最早记录为“推进、促进、鼓励”。

items.en: From Latin promovere 'move forward, advance, bring forward' = pro- 'forward' + movere 'to move'.
items.cn: 来自拉丁语 promovere“向前移、推进、带上前”= pro-“向前”+ movere“移动”。

items.en: movere also gives move, remove, motive, emotion, and moment. The family is about motion, and pro- turns it into forward motion.
items.cn: movere 还生成 move、remove、motive、emotion、moment。这个词族关乎运动，pro- 把它变成向前运动。

items.en: The senses 'raise to a higher office' and 'help forward a cause' become established.
items.cn: “提升到更高职位”与“推动某项事业”的义项确立。

items.en: Commercial promotion appears: advertising pushes goods toward buyers.
items.cn: 商业推广义出现：广告把商品推向买家。

items.en: Modern English uses promote for careers, health, products, teams, and chemical reactions, always with the same forward push.
items.cn: 现代英语用 promote 指职业、健康、产品、球队与化学反应，始终是同一个向前推动。

note.en: The first group shares the movere root and the -mote shape; the second is about verbs that also mean raising or supporting.
note.cn: 第一组共享 movere 词根与 -mote 形态，第二组看同样表示“提升”或“支持”的动词。

entries.definition: a rise in rank; a marketing campaign.
entries.definitionCN: 晋升；促销活动。

entries.definition: a person who organizes or backs an event or business.
entries.definitionCN: 发起人；承办者。

entries.definition: far away, literally 'moved back'. It is re- 'back' + movere.
entries.definitionCN: 遥远的，字面“被移开”。它是 re-“向后”+ movere。

entries.definition: to move forward or raise in rank. It overlaps promote but is less institutional.
entries.definitionCN: 向前移动或提升等级。它与 promote 重叠，但更少机构色彩。

entries.definition: to give someone confidence or help something grow. It names morale and support, not position.
entries.definitionCN: 给某人信心或助长某事。它命名士气与支持，而非职位。

entries.definition: to make something widely known. It matches the advertising sense but not the career sense.
entries.definitionCN: 使某事广为人知。它对应推销义，不对应职业义。

normalIntro.en: Real links: Latin movere 'move', the pro- 'forward' prefix, the promotion/promoter pair, and the chess and league uses.
normalIntro.cn: 真实联系：拉丁语 movere“移动”、前缀 pro-“向前”、promotion/promoter 这对词，以及国际象棋与联赛用法。

normal.en: Movere means 'move' and pro- means 'forward': promote is to move someone or something forward.
normal.cn: movere 意为“移动”，pro- 意为“向前”：promote 就是把某人或某物向前移。

normal.en: The same push serves a career, a cause, a product, and a pawn: all are moved up or forward.
normal.cn: 同一个推动服务职业、事业、产品与棋子：它们都被向上或向前推。

normal.en: Remote is re- plus movere, 'moved back'; promote is pro- plus movere, 'moved forward'. One prefix, two directions.
normal.cn: remote 是 re- 加 movere，“被移开”；promote 是 pro- 加 movere，“被推向前”。一个前缀，两个方向。

normal.en: In sport, promotion is the reward for finishing high, and relegation is its mirror image.
normal.cn: 体育中，升级是名列前茅的奖赏，降级是它的镜像。

normal.en: A catalyst promotes a reaction without being consumed: it pushes the process forward and stays.
normal.cn: 催化剂促进反应而自身不被消耗：它把过程推向前，并留在原地。

abstract.en: Advancement is a spatial metaphor: we imagine a career as a ladder and call each step a promotion.
abstract.cn: 晋升是一种空间隐喻：我们把职业想象成梯子，把每一级称作 promotion。

abstract.en: To promote an idea is to give it momentum in other minds, not merely to mention it.
abstract.cn: 推动一个理念，是给它在他者心智中的动量，而不只是提到它。

abstract.en: The chess pawn shows the metaphor literally: the lowest piece can become the highest by reaching the far rank.
abstract.cn: 国际象棋的兵把隐喻变成字面：最低的子只要走到远端，就能变成最高的子。

examples.en: She was promoted to senior manager last month.
examples.cn: 她上个月被提升为高级经理。

examples.en: The campaign promotes recycling in schools.
examples.cn: 这场运动在学校推广回收。

examples.en: Exercise promotes good health at every age.
examples.cn: 运动在各年龄段都促进健康。

dict_mnemonic.text: “扑若谋特”——扑过去谋划，把特出的人往上推 → promote 提升、促进

root: 拉丁语 promovere“向前移”，由 pro-“向前”+ movere“移动”构成；同族有 move、remove、motive、emotion。

sensesIntro.en: Nine senses of promote, all the same forward push. The push can raise a person, grow a cause, sell a product, advance a pupil, crown a pawn, or speed a reaction.
sensesIntro.cn: promote 的九个义项，都是同一个向前推动。这个推可以提升一个人、壮大一项事业、卖出产品、让学生升级、让兵升变，或加速反应。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: pushing a person or thing forward and upward.
core.cn: 核心意象：把人或物向前、向上推。

branches.en: RANK: a person, pupil, or team moves to a higher level.
branches.cn: 等级：人、学生或球队移到更高层。

branches.en: GROWTH: causes and values are given momentum in the world.
branches.cn: 成长：事业与价值在世界中获得动量。

branches.en: MARKET: goods are pushed toward buyers through publicity.
branches.cn: 市场：商品通过宣传被推向买家。

branches.en: GAME: a pawn reaches the far rank and becomes a stronger piece.
branches.cn: 游戏：兵走到远端，变成更强的子。

branches.en: PROCESS: chemistry speeds a reaction, and the archaic sense keeps the physical push.
branches.cn: 过程：化学加速反应，古义保留物理推动。

intro.en: Promote is a Latin verb. English adds -ion, -er, and -ional, and the root movere also builds move, remove, motive, and emotion.
intro.cn: promote 是拉丁动词。英语加 -ion、-er、-ional，词根 movere 还构成 move、remove、motive、emotion。

latinIntro.en: Latin promovere 'move forward' joins pro- 'forward' to movere 'move'. The same movere appears in remote (moved back), remove, and motive.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 promovere“向前移”把 pro-“向前”与 movere“移动”结合。同一个 movere 出现在 remote（移开）、remove、motive。

items.meaning: a rise in rank; a marketing campaign
items.meaningCN: 晋升；促销（-ion 构成名词）

items.meaning: one who organizes or backs something
worthy of being raised in rank
a reason that moves a person
